articleTitle: Design and Simulation of an Efficient Memristor based Full subtractor using Hybrid logic
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Memristor-based digital circuits offer a promising solution to overcome CMOS limitations in scalability, speed, and power efficiency. This research explores the design of memristors, implementing digital circuits such as NAND gate, NOR gate, NOT gate, Multiplexer, and Full Subtractors. Simulations using MATLAB and LTspice evaluate performance, highlighting advantages like fast switching, non-volatility, and energy efficiency. These circuits were designed and simulated in MATLAB and LTspice using experimentally validated HP memristor model with precise current-voltage(V-I) characteristics. Comparative analysis underscores the potential of hybrid memristor -CMOS systems for next-generation memory and computational architectures. Circuit simulations assess the impact of memristor switching properties on energy consumption, reliability, and logic gate functionality. The memristors characteristics are integrated to enhance practical relevance. By addressing the current semiconductor challenges, this work establishes a foundation for more efficient and scalable digital circuits, advancing low power, high speed applications and paving the way for future innovations in computing and memory technologies.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Smart Traffic Monitoring and Control System for Urban Areas
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The rapidly growing density of motor vehicles in the cities makes it compulsory to develop new strategies for traffic management and control. This paper presents an IoT-based traffic management system to improve the traffic flow in urban areas by utilizing the real-time modules of sensing, control and decision making. The system integrates ultrasonic sensors, Arduino UNO, GSM, Raspberry Pi, camera, traffic lights and computer vision techniques to achieve the key functionalities of calculating the traffic density, optimizing the timing of traffic lights, identification of traffic violations and recognizing the emergency vehicles. The traffic volume data has been captured across the lanes and then processed to implement the optimized duration of traffic lights to avoid the unnecessary delays. The cameras and Raspberry Pi controller detect the traffic violations by using computer vision algorithms to enforce the traffic rules. The GSM module receives the messages from emergency vehicles for priority passage and sends the information to congestion control center. The device has been fabricated, tested for expected results and found to be working fine. The experimental results illustrate optimized traffic control, identification of emergency vehicles with negligible false positives and the prediction accuracy of 93% for traffic congestions on the roads. The designed system can be used for efficient traffic management in urban areas.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Insights In To Diabetes Risk Factors And Patient Care Optimization Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Given the rising incidence of type2 diabetes worldwide, it is becoming more and more crucial to find possible origins of the condition. Finding possible reasons for this illness is still quite difficult, however. The goal of this effort is to use machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict diabetes risk factors. Diabetes mellitus is a chronic condition characterized by abnormalities in the metabolism of proteins, fats, and carbohydrates. The primary sign of diabetes is hyperglycemia or elevated blood sugar levels. This paper outlines a supervised learning technique to create efficient risk prediction tools fortheoccurrenceoftype2diabetes. A features analysis is used to examine their importance and possible connection to diabetes. The feature extraction techniques accomplished in principal component analysis (PCA) have been used to increase prediction accuracy. These elements, corresponding to the most common symptoms of diabetes that might appear gradually, are used to train and evaluate several machine learning models. Precision, Accuracy, Recall, F-Measure, and AUC are the measures used to assess and compare various machine learning models under a 5-fold cross-validation and data splitting. Both validation methods indicated that the Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) algorithms were the best-performing models.

articleTitle: Real Time Control of a Three Tank Conical System in Non Square MIMO System Configuration
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Regarding multiple non-square structures with first-order transfer function components as well as time lag, this work suggests a novel approach to construct a Smith splitting regulator with delaying adjustment utilizing internal model control (IMC). The technique suggested be implemented for controlling the configuration problem of three tank conical systems in non-square multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) initial command in addition to waiting time non-square structures, wherein is the amount of input factors surpasses than the number of outcomes, alongside the factors for input and output being two and one, respectively. This method nevertheless removes the impact that model assumption and unpredictability have on system efficiency, but it also dynamically makes up for the shortcomings of static decoupling. In other words, the real time results demonstrate that the design approach suggested in this research may greatly enhance the control system's resilience and dynamic quality. Additionally, this new approach is straightforward and simple to use. Utilizing the integral errors (ISE, IAE, ITAE) performance criteria and controller variation (TV) criteria, the design process is quantitatively assessed.

Author Keywords: non-square MIMO IMC and Performance analysis

articleTitle: Edge-enhanced YOLOv8 for Adaptive Real-time Pothole detection in smart road network
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The aim of this project has been to enhance road safety by using the inexpensive ESP32-CAM module along with YOLO V8 for pothole detection. It is possible to capture real-time photos of the road due to the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the ESP32-CAM. In terms of methodology, grayscale conversion and Canny algorithm-based edge detection techniques have been used in pre-processing to detect pothole anomalies from contours. Adding the morphological processes and filtering techniques improves the accuracy by removing noise and false positives. The processed data can be combined with GPS modules to map locations of potholes and provide drivers and local authorities with real-time alerts. Preliminary findings suggest that the system can detect potholes in different lighting and environmental conditions, which may give the system an extensive application. articleTitle: Advanced Verification Strategy for AHB-to-APB Bridge with Protocol-Aware Test Bench
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper focuses on designing and verifying an AHB-to-APB bridge, a crucial Soc component enabling seamless communication between AHB and APB peripherals. Implemented in Verilog, the design ensures optimized hardware efficiency and functionality. Verification uses a UVM-based testbench, incorporating constrained-random stimulus, assertions, and protocol-aware strategies to identify corner-case bugs and validate boundary conditions. Functional and code coverage are meticulously tracked, with the aim of 96% coverage to ensure design reliability. Additionally, assertionbased verification enhances protocol compliance by validating correct behaviour under all conditions. The modular and scalable verification framework enables reusability across protocol converters and Soc components. This project ensures the robust operation of the AHB-to-APB bridge and contributes to efficient and reusable verification methodologies in modern Soc architectures.

articleTitle: Vertical Spatial Prediction of Soil Salinity and Management Zoning for Perambalur District of Tamil Nadu, India
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Monitoring and managing soil salinity is vital due to its negative impact on agricultural production. Electrical conductivity (EC) at different profile levels is a baseline for assessing salinity and salt accumulation across soil horizons. Random Forest algorithm was applied to predict EC and Exchangeable Sodium Percentage (ESP) in Perambalur district at depths of 0–20 cm, 20–40 cm, and 40–80 cm, using 1159 soil samples obtained via conditioned Latin hypercube sampling. SCORPAN-based environmental covariates (32 nos) generate the model variables, with analysis of the percentage contribution of each environmental variable prediction process through Permutation Feature Importance analysis for identifying Elevation, Physiography, Geomorphology, Annual Mean Air Temperature, and Annual Mean Precipitation. Model performance was validated using a 70:30 holdback procedure and metrics (RMSE, NSE, and RPIQ). For EC, RMSE ranged from 0.20 to 0.28 dS m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, NSE from 0.40 to 0.58, and RPIQ from 1.06 to 1.26, respectively. For ESP, RMSE ranged from 3.40 to 3.54, NSE from 0.42 to 0.64, and RPIQ from 1.32 to 1.68. Using vertical predictions of EC and ESP, management zones were delineated via fuzzy C-means clustering at a 30 m resolution. These zones and spatial salinity distribution insights enhance the feasibility of targeted mitigation practices through informed policy decisions.

articleTitle: Design of a Versatile CMOS Synchronous Counter with Advanced Gating Techniques for Energy-Efficient Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In this paper, a synchronous up/down counter using gate driver logic and high-speed local clock generation is designed and implemented in CMOS technology. The suggested counter is perfect for digital systems that need accurate counting and timing capabilities because it operates quickly, uses little power, and is reliable. By employing gate driver logic for local clock generation, system performance is improved by reducing power consumption and delays. Comparing the suggested design to more conventional global clock distribution systems, simulation results show that it operates efficiently and synchronizes more quickly.

articleTitle: Material Comparative Study of a CrescentShaped Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna for Early Detection of Kidney Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Early diagnosis of kidney cancer helps to tailor the treatment planning and provides the patient’s prognosis. In order to diagnose cancer at an early stage, a Crescent-shaped flexible patch antenna is proposed. This paper details the design of a Novel Crescent-shaped flexible patch antenna of dimensions 56x72 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, fabricated on polyimide with a dielectric constant of 3.4 operated at 2.4GHz. Conductive materials like Silver, Aluminium, and Copper are used to fabricate three different antennas to obtain and study the maximum gain, shift in frequency, and return loss. By examining the noticeable change in the reflection coefficient and the shift in resonance frequency the proposed model can be used detect the presence of tumor in the kidney. The proposed antenna was precisely tested, using both simulation techniques and network analyzer.

articleTitle: High-Performance Optical OFDM System with Single Photon Pulsed Laser and Advanced Amplification for Long-Haul Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Improving signal transmission in Radio over Fiber (RoF) systems is crucial for enhancing performance, reducing losses. Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and RoF can be combined to create a high-performing, scalable, and flexible system for wireless and optical communication networks. OFDM divides the available bandwidth into multiple closely spaced subcarriers, each modulated with a lower-rate data stream. These subcarriers are orthogonal to each other, preventing interference and allowing the efficient use of bandwidth, whereas modulation schemes such as Quadrature Amplitude Modulation are used for each subcarrier to increase the data rate. RoF systems combine both wireless and optical links to create heterogeneous networks. The purpose of this paper is to explore the use of a Single Photon Pulsed Laser and assess its effectiveness in providing optimal performance in terms of signal integrity, transmission efficiency, and overall system performance. In particular, the Mach-Zehnder Modulator is employed for external modulation, as it demonstrates more reliable performance when combined with the OFDM modulation technique.

articleTitle: Intelligent Battery Management System using Machine Learning with Dual axis Solar Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Electric vehicles becoming more and more popular around the world as a result of the rising demand for environmentally friendly transportation. Integrating solar power into charging systems presents a viable way to support the EV charging infrastructure and lessen dependency on grid electricity. The system majorly consists of solar panels, a control unit based on raspberry pi, light sensors, a motor controller, and the battery management system. The input received by control unit in terms of illumination and directionality is provided to it by light sensors. These details are analysed to calculate an ideal position where the solar panel must be moved as determined by the control unit through the control of the motor controller The dual-axis solar tracking technology continuously aligns the solar panels with the sun's position to maximize energy collecting. The panels' horizontal and vertical axes can be dynamically adjusted to optimize amount of solar energy captured throughout the day. The BMS effectively keeps an eye on and regulates important factors like BMS guarantees optimal state-of-charge and overall battery health, improving safety and longevity.

articleTitle: Twin-Layer Deep Learning Model with IoT Integration for Intelligent Pest Detection in Smart Farming
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Smart farming needs accurate pest detection models. This research develops an efficient pest classification system using deep learning and IoT integration. An improved YOLOv8 model extracts features and detects pests. A deep neural network (DNN) classifies detected pests. The proposed Cross-Scale Attention Gradient Pruning enhances learning efficiency in both YOLOv8 and DNN. The Cross-Scale Attention Gradient Pruning method reduces redundant computations. It focuses on essential features for accurate detection and classification. This improves processing speed and reduces memory usage. The method ensures real-time pest detection in smart farming. The IoT framework collects and transmits real-time images to the deep learning model. The lightweight model allows deployment on resource-limited devices. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy than existing models. The pruning technique reduces model size while maintaining classification precision. The system detects and classifies pests in real-world farming environments. The improved YOLOv8 architecture enhances object detection with better feature extraction. The DNN classifier ensures reliable pest identification. The model outperforms conventional deep learning approaches in accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Implementation Of Humanoid Robot Using Arduino Mega
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Humanoid robots are advanced robotic systems designed to mimic human structure and movement. The robot is designed to move and perform tasks based on commands received wirelessly through a Bluetooth module (HC-05). It combines servo motors for limb movement and DC motors for wheeled navigation, controlled via an L298N motor driver. The system is powered by rechargeable batteries, ensuring continuous operation. The robot responds to user inputs via a mobile application or controller, enabling precise and flexible movement. The Arduino Mega processes real-time commands, ensuring smooth operation and quick response. The absence of an ultrasonic sensor simplifies the design while maintaining functionality through motor control. Bluetooth connectivity allows for remote control, making the system suitable for educational, automation, and assistive applications. This project showcases the integration of robotics and embedded systems for smart, wireless control.

articleTitle: EMG Signal Analysis using Improved Wigner- Ville Distribution Model And Long Short- Term Memory For Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a degenerative disease of the motor neuron function and physical ability that highlights the importance of early diagnosis to recognize ALS and improve overall outcomes. In this study, we propose a hybrid novel framework that utilizes improved Wigner-Ville Distribution (WVD) to improve time-frequency representations of electromyography (EMG) signals, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to capture spacial features of EMG signals and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to model dependencies in time. The improved WVD signals do provide a time-frequency representation that provides informative extraction of features suited to clinical features. CNNs can capture important patterns regarding the spatial features and complexity of EMG signals. The LSTM network makes use of the sequential dependencies in the EMG signal to enhance the classification of ALS. The hybrid framework conclusively outperforms existing conventional methods, proving to be a reliable and efficient means in clinical practice for ALS detection.

articleTitle: Optimized Dynamic Comparator Design for Enhanced Speed and Power Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper presents a new low-noise, Power-efficient, fast-response dynamic comparator. The comparator is implemented in two stages and employs two pre-amplifiers, which eliminates unwanted noise referred to as regenerative noise. It also utilizes Dynamic Current Reutilization to achieve speed without introducing latency. It was synthesized and implemented using 65-nm CMOS technology with a 1.2-V supply voltage. It was shown through simulation that the design had an offset standard deviation of just 8 mV, i.e., three times less than an average design. The comparator is also very energy-efficient and high-speed. It only uses a maximum of 67 femto joules (fJ) of power and has an average delay of 70 picoseconds (ps). The undesired noise produced kickback noise, is also only 5.5 mV, which is ten times less than in traditional designs with a 500 MHz clock frequency. All of these enhancements make this comparator highly appropriate for use in applications where low power and high-speed operation are needed with low noise and latency.

articleTitle: Low Power CMOS Folded Electro Cascode Amplifier Design for Electrocardiogram Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper presents the designing of folded electro cascode amplifier which is mainly used in electrocardiogram (ECG) applications. The ECG front end amplifier which is used nowadays are sensitive to noisy environments which can vary the signal produced. The proposed amplifier which is highly stable in noisy environments because of using electro cascode stage is used in the proposed amplifier. It consumes low power and low voltage which can enhance the better performance and also low noise. The amplifier is designed to operate in 1.2 V. The design is implemented in 45 nm CMOS technology and the layout design has been designed in cadence virtuoso software. The simulation results shows that the amplifier is suitable for low power applications and can be used for wearable devices.

articleTitle: Advancing Smart Farming with UAV-Based Deep Learning for Proactive Wheat Disease Management
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Wheat diseases are a huge risk to the food security of the world and can result in extreme yield loss in case they are not diagnosed and treated at an early stage. Previously, disease identification required manual scanning, which is labor intensive, time-consuming, and inaccurate. The project shows a real-time, scalable, and automated wheat disease detection system with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), multispectral sensing, and deep learning. The system described above is unlike the conventional ground-based methods, the model uses aerial imagery collected using UAVs in conjunction with deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), specifically fine-tuned VGG19, to enhance scalability and accuracy. Grad-CAM visualization is also integrated to make predictions from models interpretable by farmers. In addition, the system incorporates real-time processing as well as IoT for automated early disease intervention alerting. The combination of large-scale monitoring, high-accuracy disease detection, and farmer-friendly deployment, this project fills important gaps in existing research with a pioneering, field-application solution for precision agriculture. Experimental results show high detection accuracy, proving its robustness under varying environmental conditions. This technology allows farmers to obtain real-time information, enabling timely disease management and sustainable wheat production.

articleTitle: Tow-Thomas-Controlled Single-Phase Solar Powered Microgrids: Performance Evaluation in Grid-Tied and Standalone Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The following paper proposes a well-planned microgrid system aimed at damping harmonics and enabling smooth transitions from grid-tied to standalone operation. The setup comprises a photovoltaic (PV) solar generation system, a voltage-fed converter, and a battery driven energy storage unit. To control a voltage fed converter, we use gate pulses generated by the Tow-Thomas algorithm, ensuring efficiency and accuracy. For optimal solar power tracking, system uses the Perturb and Observe (P&O) method with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) system to regulate the duty cycle of the DC-DC step up converter. During grid failures, a switch transition logic (STL) based controller, transitions the system from grid-reliant to self-sufficient operation, ensuring uninterrupted power supply to critical loads. Shunt compensation is connected to the microgrid for harmonic damping, load current balancing, and better power quality control at the point of common interfacing (PCI) . The effectiveness and reliability of the outlined system is implemented and analyzed under various loads and different irradiation conditions.

articleTitle: Inferred Lattice Recursive Least Squares Filter with DCT-Hadamard Pre-Processing Technique for Speech Enhancement in Digital Hearing Aid
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Digital hearing aids is an important support for hearing impaired person. In real-world scenarios, hearing aids often encounter various environmental noise sources that can interfere with speech perception. The proposed work addresses this issue using the Inferred Lattice Recursive Least Squares (ILRLS) algorithm for speech enhancement in hearing aid applications. ILRLS algorithm is applied to the context of digital hearing aids with the objective of enhancing the speech signal while suppressing background noise. Speech samples are collected for the NOIZEUS, SpEAR and TIMIT database for experimentation and validation. The speech samples are pre-processed using Discrete Cosine Transform - Hadamard hybrid algorithm to arrange samples with respect to its frequency components, and to adapt in the algorithm effectively. Effectiveness of the proposed work is assessed by metrics like signal-to-noise ratio, perceptual evaluation of speech Quality, and Mean Square Error. Subjective listening tests were also conducted to gather user feedback. The proposed method significantly enhances both speech quality and intelligibility in noisy environments. The adaptive nature of ILRLS allows it to adapt to changing noise conditions, making it well-suited for digital hearing aids

Author Keywords: Inferred Lattice Recursive Least Square Algorithm

articleTitle: Stacking-Based Machine Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Embedded System Network Traffic
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Embedded systems are increasingly deployed in critical infrastructures, making them prime targets for cyber threats and malicious activities. Traditional embedded security techniques often fail to protect against sophisticated network-based attacks in real-time. In this paper, a stacking-based machine learning approach for identifying network traffic anomalies in embedded devices is proposed. It uses a dataset that includes regular and unusual network traffic patterns. For better detection, the proposed model uses stacking ensemble learning with several base classifiers. Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) are chosen as basic learners. These approaches are chosen as they can discriminate between regular and harmful network activity better. After integrating these basic learners, a meta-classifier refines the final predictions by learning from their collective outputs. With 94.4% accuracy, the stacking ensemble technique detects network abnormalities better than individual models. In contrast to solo classifiers, stacking decreases false positives and enhances anomaly identification. In embedded systems, this work delivers scalable and effective security threat detection. A stacking-based architecture can be utilized for industrial control, IoT, and vehicle security.

articleTitle: Voice Bot for Visually Impaired Persons using NLP
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: As digital platforms continue to dominate daily tasks, visually impaired users face substantial barriers in accessing these tools, performing everyday activities, and navigating their physical environments safely. Our proposed system leverages advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and voice recognition technology to create an intuitive, user-centered solution. The voice-controlled interface allows users to perform tasks such as browsing the internet, managing their schedules, sending messages, tracking fitness, and staying socially connected. By minimizing the reliance on visual input, the system provides a more inclusive way for visually impaired individuals to engage with the digital world. Additionally, the system includes a real-time obstacle detection feature that uses auditory feedback to alert users of potential hazards, thus enhancing safety during physical navigation. AI algorithms enable the system to adapt to user-specific needs, providing context-aware, personalized assistance, and continuously learning from user interactions. This project not only focuses on improving daily functionality and user experience but also emphasizes ease of use and accessibility. Future developments will involve the integration of advanced sensors, as well as more sophisticated machine learning algorithms to further enhance the system’s performance. Continuous feedback from users will be critical in refining the system, ensuring it remains responsive, reliable, and effective in promoting a higher degree of independence for visually impaired users.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Smart Caching for Optimized Web Performance and Reduced Latency
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The increasing demand for faster and more efficient web browsing has led to significant challenges in caching mechanisms. Traditional caching algorithms, such as Least Recently Used (LRU) and Least Frequently Used (LFU), rely on static rules and do not adapt to dynamic user behavior or real-time network conditions. This research introduces an AI-driven smart caching system that utilizes Machine Learning (ML) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) to predict frequently accessed content and optimize cache allocation dynamically. The proposed model continuously learns from user interaction patterns, network latency and content popularity to enhance cache hit ratios and minimize redundant server requests. By implementing deep learning-based predictive caching, the system reduces web page load time, bandwidth usage and computational overhead on web servers and Content Delivery Networks (CDNs). A comparative analysis with traditional caching methods demonstrates improved performance in terms of response time, storage efficiency and network bandwidth utilization. This study highlights the potential of AI-powered caching strategies in modern web applications, cloud services and mobile browsing environments. The research contributes to the growing field of AI-driven network optimization by presenting a scalable and adaptive caching mechanism. Future developments could include integrating federated learning for privacy-preserving cache predictions and extending the model to support edge computing and 5G-based web infrastructure.

articleTitle: MOODPLUS - Personalized Mental Health Recommendation Software Solution
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Mental health is a very real growing concern for millions of people in today's era now even working professionals and the common masses. Stress, anxiety and emotional burnout can adversely affect personal health as well as performance. The MOODPLUS is an AI-driven emotion-affordable system that gives personalized recommendations for entertainment and activities based on mood, to help individuals better manage their emotions. MOODPLUS uses state-of-the-art BERT with the training on Twitter Emotion Dataset to identify emotions from user input. Depending on the emotion found, activities like watching a movie / reading a book, listening to music or relaxation exercises can be recommended. These suggestions are age and taste specific as well as suited for current emotional state so that users get helpful suggestions. MOODPLUS improves the recommendations over time it uses Reinforcement learning, so that it learns from user returned reward and improves its recommendations.

articleTitle: Pap Smear Image Segmentation and Classification Methods For Cervical Cancer Detection Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Cervical cancer ranks as a major cause of death among women globally, making essential for effective treatment. The automated examination of Pap smear images through sophisticated machine learning and deep learning methods has notably enhanced diagnostic precision. This study conducts a comprehensive review of segmentation and classification methods utilized for Pap smear images, with an emphasis on UNet and Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks (R-CNN) for segmentation, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for classification, along with Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) for optimization. U-Net has shown remarkable effectiveness in segmenting both cytoplasm and nuclei from Pap smear images, thus enhancing feature extraction for classification purposes [3]. Likewise, RCNN has proven to be adept at detecting and pinpointing abnormal cervical cells, yielding accurate segmentation outcomes [6]. In terms of classification, SVM has been frequently employed because of its ability to differentiate between normal and abnormal cells based on the features extracted [10]. CNN, utilizing deep learning, has exhibited exceptional performance in autonomously learning structured features for the precise classification of cervical cells [12]. Furthermore, SGD has been vital in optimizing deep learning architectures, enhancing both training efficiency and convergence rate [15]. The combination of these methods has resulted in improved accuracy and reliability in the detection of cervical cancer, promoting early diagnosis and minimizing the manual workload in pathology laboratories. This review sheds light on the latest developments in segmentation and classification approaches, underscoring their influence on enhancing cervical cancer screening.

articleTitle: Enhancing Machine Learning Classifiers for Prostate Cancer Detection through Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Prostate cancer causes most death among men, which makes early detection very important. In this work, we use microarray gene expression data, which contains a large amount of information, to help detect prostate cancer early. To handle this complex data, we use different methods like machine learning, feature selection, and dimensionality reduction. Chi<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Probability Density Function (Chi<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> PDF) and Cuckoo Search (CS) are used to reduce the number of features, while Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Harmonic Search (HS) help choose the most useful ones. We test five classifiers—Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), SVM with RBF kernel, Expectation Maximization (EM), Linear Regression, and Nonlinear Regression—with and without feature selection. The results show that using SVM-RBF with feature selection gives the highest accuracy for detecting prostate cancer early

Author Keywords: Gene data and Prostate cancer detection

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Application to Detect and Diagnose Metabolic Encephalopathy
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Brain health plays a major role in human life to recognize their complete prospective over the life course stating the brain functionality which includes sensory, behavioral, cognitive, social-emotional and motor domains regardless of the existence or nonexistence of disorders. If there exists a brain dysfunction due to chemical imbalances in the blood, it is named as Metabolic Encephalopathy. This chemical imbalances occur due to the systematic illness such as diabetes, kidney or liver disease which may disturb mental states and if not treated in right time may lead to permanent brain damage. The role of artificial intelligence in medical field is showing its significant growth in recent years. This document showcases deep learning techniques in the diagnosis of metabolic encephalopathy.

articleTitle: Impact of Spatial Context on Characterization of Activities of Daily Living Using sEMG Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Assessment of activities of daily living is an important method for evaluating a) the overall health of individuals living in smart health-care homes and b) progress in the rehabilitation process for stroke patients. The classification of ADL is an important component of such assessment methods. In practice, surface electromyography (sEMG) signals can be used to automatically classify ADLs in real-world scenarios. Even though, under laboratory conditions, the classifiers perform well, their widespread usage is limited by the measurement context. Specifically, models that perform well on data from a specific context may fail with data from a different context. In this study, the focus is on the spatial context of measurement in terms of the environment of ADL, reaching distance between the subject and the objects of ADL, and body positions. sEMG signals are collected from 10 subjects while performing ADL in two distinct environments, such as the kitchen and workspace, under two body postures and three reaching distances. Features based on time domain (TD) statistics and log moments in the frequency domain are extracted and classified using the random forest model. The machine learning experiments on ADL classification are conducted in two scenarios; when the environmental context is 1) assumed to be known and 2) estimated from the data. The key finding in this work is that the ADL classification is consistently higher in the first scenario and basic DL frameworks fail to perform well in both scenarios. Finally, from the statistical tests, it is determined that i) reaching distance has a statistically significant impact on the ADL classification in the workspace environment and ii) body position has a significant impact on classification performance of the most of the activities.

articleTitle: Intelligent Crop Yield Prediction Using IoT and Optimized Deep Learning for Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The accurate prediction of crop yield plays an important role in sustainable agriculture. Traditional prediction methods depend on historical data and general environmental assumptions. These methods lack accuracy and fail to adapt to real-time field conditions. The proposed research develops an intelligent system that integrates IoT sensors with an optimized deep-learning model for precise yield prediction. The system collects real-time data using IoT sensors that measure soil moisture, temperature, humidity, pH, and light intensity. A cloud-based platform processes this data with a MobileNet-Inspired LSTM model. A self-adaptive Adam optimizer enhances training efficiency by adjusting learning rates dynamically. The model analyzes real-time environmental conditions along with future weather data from an external API. A web dashboard presents predictions to users, allowing better decision-making. The proposed method solves key challenges in yield prediction by improving data accuracy. The integration of IoT ensures real-time monitoring. The MobileNet-Inspired LSTM model improves prediction accuracy while maintaining efficiency. The self-adaptive Adam optimizer accelerates training, reducing errors in yield estimation. The system is tested on coconut, rice, guava, and papaya yield datasets. The results show that the proposed model achieves an R-squared score above 0.90 for most crops, indicating strong predictive performance. Compared to existing methods, the proposed approach reduces mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and root mean square error (RMSE), proving its reliability. The research enhances precision agriculture by providing an accurate, real-time, and scalable crop yield prediction system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Single-Channel Speech Processing With Advanced Noise-Reduction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of a CNN-based U-Net architecture to enhance the quality of speech signals degraded by noise. The goal here is to measure how much clarity and intelligibility of speech improves for children who might be having difficulty perceiving speech because of background urban noise. An extensive experiment was performed on a dataset which had clean speech from RAVDESS and the urban background from UrbanSound8K.Using the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), the audio samples were changed to time frequency representation and were applied to a U-Net network. Various objective measures were utilized to evaluate improvements such as the signal to noise ratio (SNR), Itakura-Saito distance, RMSE, or the short-time objective intelligibility (STOI). They were well contrasted with standard filtering techniques such as Wiener filtering or Weinberg masking. The improvements in these technologies were witnessed with an increase in the STOI score which increased from 0.71 to 0.83 which indicates an improvement in the speech quality. In addition, using the Mean Opinion Score (MOS) which asks listeners to provide their qualitative assessments of the enhanced audio signals in terms of certain topics. With the discussions, it was confirmed that U-Net is useful in speech improvement and quality enhancement through noise reduction. The experiments revealed that the performance of the fuse deep CNN U-Net architecture is superior to legacy approaches for restoring the quality of speech in the presence of background noise. These insights may inform the design and development of changing amplifiers and other audio systems to assist communication in ‘difficult’ listening conditions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electric Vehicle Integration with Renewable Energy through Advanced Energy Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The growth of electric vehicles (EVs) places a demand for efficient systems of energy management to enable proper integration with renewable energy resources. Current systems are poorly equipped to extract solar power for charging and to ensure one-way energy flows from cars to the grid and back (V2G and G2V). For instance, problems arise regarding the conversion of energy at charging and discharge times, which leads to energy loss and decreased battery operation. An advanced energy system with solar harvesting energy, a DC-DC converter, and MPPT algorithms allows for seamless energy transfer between the source and consumer sides. A dedicated controller controls and manages the energy levels with a charging cycle and allows vehicle-to-grid services to help improve energy efficiency while lowering costs and prolonging the life of the batteries by ensuring grid stability. This solution aims to establish an ecosystem of sustainable energy and supports a greener, more resilient energy infrastructure by maximising the use of renewable energy and promoting EV-grid integration.

articleTitle: Antipodal Antenna for Smart Vehicular applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Antipodal Vivaldi is capable of operating within the gigahertz frequency range, which is well-suited for 5G and future applications. One of the biggest applications of 5G is autonomous cars. The Vivaldi antenna is designed in a way that has four ports that generates four directional beams and effectively identifies obstacles within a 90-degree angle." This is placed in the four corners of the car to detect the obstacles in every corner with an angle of 90 degrees. The designed antenna is then simulated by using the ADS software and with the result it is validated that this designed antenna successfully provides full 90-degree view around each corner.

articleTitle: The Role of THz Technology in Enhancing Cellular Mobile Based FANET for UAVs in 6G
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The interface of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) into 6G networks using terahertz (THz) communication it’s provides a significant advancement in UAV connectivity, enabling high-quality and reliable communication. These capabilities have broad applications in military and civilian domains and emergency applications, disaster management. This paper addresses critical challenges in Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs), specifically related to coverage range, data transmission efficiency, and power consumption in UAV-to-UAV communications. Two major limitations of UAV-to-UAV communication in FANETs are identified and mitigated through the implementation of cellular interfaces and THz communication methods and the power consumptions improved to Solar panel, and also maintain the weight of the UAVs. The proposed solutions enhance the coverage range, improve data transmission, and optimize power consumption, making UAV communications in 6G networks more efficient and effective.

articleTitle: Classification of Diseases in Mango Leaves based on deep learning using CNN model
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Mango leaf diseases cause great harm to mango production in productivity and quality. It is crucial for early and accurate detection of disease to facilitate management and prevention. In this paper, we utilize EfficientNet-B7, MobileNet, and ResNet-152 to introduce a deep learning-based method for automatically classifying mango leaf diseases. The dataset is made up of 60% train, 20% test, and 20% val. For model generalization and prevention of overfitting, extensive data augmentation methods are used in combination with L1_L2 regularization on fully connected layers. The models are learned at the learning rate 0.0001 and with early stopping utilizing the Adam optimizer to avoid overfitting. Measurement of performance for accuracy, confusion matrix, and classification reports display the efficiency with which the resulting models perform. As per experiment results, Utilizing the test dataset, EfficientNet-B7 gives an accuracy of 98.87%, MobileNet has an accuracy of 78%, and ResNet-152 attains an accuracy of 92%. The model's high accuracy proves the worth of the model in precision agriculture, a helpful and scalable alternative to automated plant disease diagnoses for mango farmers.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Automatic Plant Watering System: A Real-Time Implementation and Verification Using Xilinx
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The recent automated irrigation systems rely mainly on microcontrollers, which possess serious drawbacks such as latency, sequential processing, and inefficiency in real-time application. This results in a delayed response to the requirements of plants, increased wastage of water, and high power consumption. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an FPGA-based automatic plant watering system that provides real-time decision-making, parallel execution, and optimized resource utilization. The novelty of this work lies in the fact that it implements the control logic in hardware so as to guarantee ultra-fast response and accurate irrigation based on real-time soil moisture data. Processing can be done faster, reducing computation overhead, by utilizing FPGA as opposed to other methods. Simulation and hardware verification are ensured using Xilinx software for accuracy and dependability. Experimental results show lower water wastage, improved energy efficiency, and enhanced automation, making this approach highly suitable for smart agriculture applications.

articleTitle: Residue Number System Enveloped Configurable Hardware Mutual Authentication Protocol
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Cryptographic hardware plays a significant role in realizing secure systems. In E-Health applications, the rapid advancement of IoT technology faces severe issues with unauthorized access to patient records. Authentication is a significant problem in RFID-IoT technology. The primary purpose of this work is to emphasize the security threats posed by hardware devices and develop a novel RFID-enabled IoT Mutual Authentication Protocol (MAP). The Residue Number System (RNS) platform is used to evolve the protocol for the entity identification system by using parallel Dual Modulus {2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>±1} Multiplier Function (DMMF) design, which is the core element and configurable. The architectures are designed and described using Verilog HDL, and a performance analysis is performed for TSMC CMOS 180 nm, 90nm, and 45 nm technology. FPGA implementation of Residue Number System Mutual Authentication Protocol (RMAP) is ported in Zynq (XC7Z020CLG484-1). From the analysis, RMAP prevents various attacks, which can be efficiently utilized for secure wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid TransUNet and Attention U-Net for AI-Based Colonoscopy Polyp Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Colonoscopy remains the gold standard for the detection of polyps and the early detection of colorectal cancer. Automated polyp identification based on deep learning can reduce human error and improve diagnosis accuracy. This study proposes a hybrid model that combines Attention U-Net as the decoder and TransUNet as the encoder to enhance polyp segmentation. The encoder uses transformer-based global feature extraction, while the decoder uses attention techniques to refine the segmentation mask. A hybrid loss function that combines Dice and Focal loss is used to improve boundary precision and address class imbalance. Better segmentation performance is demonstrated by experimental tests on the CVC dataset, where the proposed model outperforms traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Near Field XL-MIMO System using SWOMP Channel Estimation for Uniform Linear Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: MIMO system with extremely large number of array antennas is commonly used in 5G/6G communications. The near field electromagnetic spherical wase is a dominating field in the XL-MIMO system and it involves both Line of Sight (LoS) and Non-Line of Sight (NLoS) path components between transmitter and receiver. Here, Uniform Linear Array (ULA) antenna is considered at both ends. The channel model for the LoS and NLoS path components are derived by considering the sparsity and polar domain representation in this paper. The channel estimation is performed for the near field components using Simultaneous Weighted Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (SWOMP) algorithm and the results are compared with existing channel estimation techniques.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of Virtual Emotional Support Platforms: Approaches and Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The quick rise in worldwide mental health problems alongside increasing population interest in customizable healthcare leads to a clear necessity for modern alternatives which deliver immediate emotional assistance. The Emoticare app delivers a digital emotional assistance program that unites artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud platforms into an expandable platform which makes mental wellness services accessible and reactive. The application implements three essential features that track personal moods while offering individualized emotional evaluations and personalized recommendations which form a complete emotional guidance system. Emoticare utilizes AI capabilities to evaluate user submissions before giving individualized recommendations about self-care activities and exercise routines along with social network suggestions and stress-related methods. The app features real-time notifications as well as emergency alerts for close contacts and profession-based mood-enhancing interventions within its comprehensive adaptive support system. This research examines the Emoticare app design along with its functional aspects and examines its potential effects by using findings from academic literature focusing on emotional support solutions, virtual agents and AI-based mental health technology. Emoticare delivers a solution to reduce emotional distress by offering users personalized emotional support which adapts to their current contexts regardless of their location.

articleTitle: Empowering Food Safety with Blockchain: A new Era of Organic Food Supply Chain Management
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Blockchain Technology is valued for its ability to document and distribute transactions in an enduring, jumbled record. Right now, food supply data is stored in a single central system, which can be easily hacked or changed by corrupt officials, leading to fake or expired products being sold to consumers. With Blockchain, every step in the supply chain management supplying of food products from raw material suppliers to manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and finally consumers is secure, transparent, and tamper-proof. Each transaction (like sending food from one place to another) is stored in blocks with a unique hash code, making it impossible to alter. The system also includes Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to predict future demand for products, helping suppliers, manufacturers, consumers plan better and KMeans cluster also used to recommend the related food items of the purchased product. Consumers and government officials can use a product ID to check the entire history of a food item.

articleTitle: Implementing Feature Extraction and GA based Feature Selection for Fingerprint-Iris and Fingerprint-Face
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: To identify the physiological and behavioral parameters of a specific person, biometrics are used. It implements several characteristics such as faces, iris, fingerprints or retinas to capture the identity. A multimodal biometric system uses a combination of two or more traits that are not forgotten, copied or stolen. Several discriminant features are extracted from samples which is represented in a feature vector. The resultant feature vector is of the order of high dimensionality which causes computational complexity and impairs the performance of classifiers. To rectify this, feature selection methods are introduced to obtain a subset of optimal features. This paper presents a multimodal biometric framework based on fingerprint, iris and face. Feature extraction is done by Gabor filter, Local Tetra Pattern and feature selection is done by Genetic Algorithm (GA).

articleTitle: Soundscape Identification of Endangered Bird Species using Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In this paper, bird vocalization, a key indicator for species identification, is a valuable tool for studying avian population, especially for endangered species whose population is difficult to monitor through traditional methods. In this paper presents an automated system dedicated to identify the endangered bird species through the analysis of bird vocalizations using a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory model. As compared to traditional approaches, the BiLSTM architecture is particularly apt for this task since it can learn audio data patterns by processing information in both forward and backward temporal directions, enhancing classification accuracy in scenarios where sound patterns may vary. This proposed system also aims to provide a vital tool for conservationists, ecologists, and researchers, offering a scalable solution for tracking avian population trends.

articleTitle: AI Framework for Fruit Quality Assessment: Integrating CNN-Based Spoilage Detection, Price Estimation, and LLM-Powered Insights
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The AI utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) combined with Large Language Models (LLMs) to deliver complete fruit-quality evaluation which includes spoilage detection and price assessment. Through deep learning image analysis the system identifies different ripeness stages of fruits at high speed which results in fast spoiled produce detection. The efficiency of the system increases because of LLM functionalities that deliver important product shelf life instructions while supplying preservation methods and proper usage guidelines. The price calculation system employs data-driven rules to measure product worth based on ripeness indicators which creates balanced pricing structure for suppliers and customers. A coalition of advanced evaluation methods and AI automation systems generates optimal fruit quality testing which enhances market evaluations and retail point-of-sale assessments. The proposed method enables both precise and efficient fruit classification as well as promotes sustainable consumption through waste reduction to enhance buying choices.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Hand Exoskeleton for Elbow Rehabilitation Using IMU Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper describes a new upper-limb exoskeleton designed for rehabilitation purpose targeted at enhancing the Sports-related injuries or Total Elbow Arthroplasty or other kinesiology-related disorders. The exoskeleton uses advanced IMU sensors to track the bio-signals, such as finger movement. The adaptive control algorithms of the system ensure that motions are tailored to the user's rehabilitation needs, fostering sensorimotor rehabilitation and improving motor coordination. Real-time data analytics technique is used to optimize the therapy process and adjust interventions based on patient progress. The exoskeleton is designed for ease of use and patient comfort, supporting functional independence and accelerating recovery by facilitating motor memory and improving joint mobility. This work proves the great possibility of combining robot-assisted therapy and wearable technology for rehabilitation in upper limb paralysis by offering an approach for patients with neurological and musculoskeletal conditions.

articleTitle: Enhanced Plant Pest Classification by Leveraging CBAM Attention in ResNet-9
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to identifying plant pests, utilizing the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) in conjunction with the ResNet-9 architecture. The study is relevant to current issues regarding pest identification, as it aims to achieve accurate and timely rates since plant pests pose serious threats to agriculture and food security. Thus, the proposed CBAM-ResNet-9 model achieves better classification accuracy and efficiency than existing models that utilize attention mechanisms to highlight relevant image features. Transfer learning utilizes pre-trained architectures to fine-tune the model, while data augmentation helps prevent overfitting through image enhancements such as rotation, scaling, and translation. A comprehensive analysis has been conducted on publicly available pest image datasets in comparison to the performance of state-of-the-art CBAMResNet-9 models under scrutiny. The experimental results prove that the proposed model is superior to various popularly used architectures in terms of efficacy for classifying different species of pests. Such results may inspire confidence in this approach for practical implementation in agricultural contexts, enabling farmers to detect and manage pests early.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Customized Convolutional Neural Network based Cardiac Health Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Collectively, Cardio Vascular Diseases (CVDs) are the most dangerous global threat to human health. Timely and accurate cardiovascular disease (CVD) diagnosis is essential for saving lives. This paper proposes a deep learning-based approach for a heart health assessment system that uses a customized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model to classify and detect cardiac abnormalities in MRI scans. Highly distinguishing normal and pathological conditions is achieved using a system leveraging Customized CNN feature extraction capabilities. The proposed custom CNN involved a diverse dataset for training, which includes both healthy and diseased ones, to enhance cross-case robustness. Appropriate use of the proposed model can reduce the challenges of diagnosing late-stage cardiovascular disease (CVD) and promote preventive healthcare strategies by offering a contactless, costeffective healthcare solution. The proposed CNN model yields an accuracy of 85.06% in identifying patients of different categories.

articleTitle: Dynamic AI Tissue Analysis For Enhanced Medical Diagnosis using TSDM
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The aim of the study is to propose TSDM-Net, a model that enhances tissue analysis accuracy through adaptation to various tissue types, and compare its performance with conventional CNN models. In this research, there are two groups. Group 1 is the CNN with attention based on the CAMELYON16 dataset, with annotated lymph node WSIs, while Group 2 is the TSDM-Net with the Break-His dataset, with benign and malignant samples of breast cancer. Preprocessing included color normalization, resizing to 512×512 pixels, and augmentation processes such as rotation, flipping, and contrast changes. The TSDM AI model performed better than the CNN model in separating healthy and diseased tissues, with a 94% accuracy and substantial improvement in precision, recall, and F1-score over 20 epochs of training. The precision (0.95) of the TSDM improved from 0.8000 to 0.9000, recall (0.94) from 0.7800 to 0.8800, and F1-score (0.945) from 0.7900 to 0.8900 at a significance level of 0.0056. In this work, it is noted that the combination of AI tissue analysis and Time-Series Data Mining (TSDM) greatly improves medical diagnostics, especially in the detection of early diseases, by enhancing the analysis and interpretation of intricate tissue data.

articleTitle: High-efficiency CNTFET-based Inverter and Pass Transistor Design for Hamming Code Encoder and Decoder for Fault-Tolerant Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: To create error-free digital data transfer, this investigation outlines the design of a Hamming code encoder and decoder circuit that combines inverter-based pass transistor logic and CNTFET techniques. The proposed logic is a revolutionary approach to low-power VLSI circuit design. Compared to other logic techniques in the literature, this approach provides a superior trade-off between power, delay, and area while maintaining a low level of circuit complexity. The proposed technique is used to design circuit topologies for Hamming code encoders and decoders, and the HSPICE Tool is used to simulate these circuits in 32nm technology. The advantages of the inverter-based pass transistor logic and CNTFET techniques are examined in this paper concerning designs made using CMOS logic types.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Classification Models for Respiratory Disease Detection Using Wiener-Ville Distribution Features
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The respiratory rate is a vital physiological metric for evaluating an individual's health, and its precise measurement is critical in clinical diagnostics. Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals offer a non-invasive and economical method for assessing respiratory activity. Nevertheless, owing to their vulnerability to noise and motion distortions, effective feature extraction and classification methods are essential for dependable respiratory detection. This study utilizes Wiener-Ville Distribution (WVD) for feature extraction, capturing the time-frequency attributes of respiratory-induced fluctuations in PPG data. A variety of classification methodologies, such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Expectation-Maximization (EM), Bayesian Linear Discriminant Classifier (BLDC), EM-PCA, and Harmonic Search (HS), are assessed for their efficacy. Experimental results indicate that the Harmonic Search (HS) classifier attains superior accuracy, surpassing alternative approaches through the efficient optimization of feature selection and classifier parameters. The suggested method underscores the efficacy of HS as the optimal classifier gives prominent accuracy of 95.12% and a minimum error rate of 4.88%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Glacial Lake Monitoring Through CNN-Based UNet Models in a Streamlit Application
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Glacial lake monitoring is important to learn about climate change and to address challenges such as GLOFs in the future. This paper presents an improved UNet model based on CNN applied to a Streamlit application for glacial lake monitoring. The system takes input of both image and csv datasets, divides glacial lakes, computes the rates of growth and generates risk along with alerts in real time. The results are stored in the cloud, in Google Firebase shall be added, and the report is generated automatically. Through the application, the users are allowed to upload images or ask questions with parameters’ help, improving the utilization of glacial lake studies.

articleTitle: Novel Hybrid Feature Extraction for Enhanced Liver Abnormality Detection using Bio-Inspired Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The early and precise identification of liver abnormality is essential for better patient care and enhanced prognosis. Conventional diagnostic approaches, including biopsies and imaging techniques, may be invasive, protracted, and necessitate specialist analysis. This research introduces an innovative hybrid feature extraction method integrated with bio-inspired classifiers to improve the classification of liver disorders. The method employs ultrasonic images, to detect cirrhotic patterns and categorize liver abnormalities. In this work the hybrid Fast Hadamard EHO techniques is used for feature extraction. The five classifiers such as Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), DFA, Firefly, Harmonic Search and hybrid algorithm such as Firefly GMM and Harmonic search GMM were used for classification of liver abnormality. The Hybrid classifier Harmonic GMM gives prominent accuracy of 96.43% and a minimum error rate of 3.57%.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Emotion Classification of BCI Data Using Autoencoder-Based Feature Extraction and Stacked Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Being a vital component, Emotion classification is used in several applications such as mental health monitoring, human-computer interaction, and affective computing. Recently, machine learning and deep learning techniques have been successfully applied to emotion classification in Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) systems for attaining improved results as compared to traditional classification approaches. This paper introduces a novel hybrid Deep Learning framework that employs an Autoencoder-based feature extraction with a stacked Ensemble learning approach for enhancing classification performance. Herein, an autoencoder is utilized as an unsupervised feature extractor for learning a compact latent representation of EEG-based emotion data. Then, the extracted features are fed into two-base classifiers, namely Random Forest and Deterministic Weight Medication-Extreme Learning Machine. The resultant predictions are then combined using a meta-learning model (Logistic Regression). This means that the hierarchical learning strategy improves the robustness and generalization capabilities of the model. In this way, an accuracy of 98.126% is obtained using the proposed framework for emotion classification. This demonstrates the framework's effectiveness in capturing complex emotion patterns for EEG classification. The attained results showcase the significant improvement in classification performance achieved by integrating deep feature extraction and an ensemble-based hybrid model as compared with the standalone models.

articleTitle: Design, modeling and comparative analysis of SRAM performance and functionality under the Subthreshold regime for various technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: SRAM is widely recognized for its high storage density and fast access time, making it an essential component in VLSI chips. Its ease of use and minimal standby leakage contribute to its extensive application across various domains. In recent years, the increasing demand for secure and reliable user systems has further expanded its use beyond communication technologies to sectors such as transportation, industry, healthcare, and automotive systems. A CMOS-based SRAM cell is particularly advantageous due to its low power consumption and reduced read/write time. This article focuses on a 6T SRAM cell, known for its efficient use of power, space, and processing time during data operations. As a type of random-access memory, SRAM retains data for extended periods without requiring frequent circuit refreshes. This paper presents a performance analysis of a 6T SRAM cell implemented in 180nm, 90nm, and 45nm technology nodes, evaluating its write time (propagation delay) using the Cadence tool. The objective is to design a 6T SRAM structure that minimizes delay, as SRAM cells occupy a significant portion of a memory chip's area.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Machine Learning Classifiers for Detecting Heart Rate Variations from PPG Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper is going to discuss about the detection of heart disorder due to variation of heart rate, and also analyze the different classifiers performance in the finding of the disorder. The five statistical features like mean, skewness, variance, kurtosis and the correlation of PPG signal is considered in this work of PO2 measurement. The PPG features will indirectly indicate the condition of heart rate .The classifiers such as SDC, Firefly, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Kernel PCA, Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), PCA Firefly are used in the classification of normal and abnormal heart rate disorder from PPG signal feature. The parameters accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, Error Rate, PI are used to analyze the performance of the classifiers. The classifier that obtained superior performance is the focus of the findings, as it indicates its effectiveness in comparison to other classifiers.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Classifiers for Liver Cirrhosis Detection Using Fast Hadamard-EHO Transform Features
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Liver cirrhosis is a gradual and irreversible disorder that impairs liver function, frequently resulting in serious complications if not identified promptly. Conventional diagnostic approaches, including biopsies and imaging techniques, may be invasive, protracted, and necessitate specialist analysis. This research introduces a soft computing based technique for the detection of liver cirrhosis, utilizing sophisticated machine learning algorithms and medical imaging analysis. The method employs ultrasonic images, to detect cirrhotic patterns and categorize liver abnormalities. In this work the hybrid Fast Hadamard EHO techniques is used for feature extraction. The five classifiers such as Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Dragon Fly algorithm, Harmonic Search and hybrid algorithm such as Dragon fly GMM and Harmonic search GMM were used for classification of liver abnormality. The Hybrid classifier Harmonic GMM gives prominent accuracy of 96.43% and a minimum error rate of 3.57%.

articleTitle: AgroInsight Pro: Sustainable Agriculture Analytics & Decision Support System using GEN-AI
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Farmers today face massive issues. Weather conditions the future, the water level is low, and we have to generate more food for more people. Traditional farming practices which were appropriate for our grandparents aren’t adequate anymore. That’s why we developed AgroInsight Pro. This emerging technology utilizes AI to guide farmers to better decision-making. It collects valuable data like soil conditions, weather forecasting, crop yields, as well as evidence of infestation on plants. After that interprets all this information into simple, actionable advice that farmers can use immediately. We pilot-tested AgroInsight Pro with a farmer group, and the result was great. They used 25% less resources (such water, fertilizers, and pesticides and lost 30% less crop to diseases that would otherwise have been preventable. It was, according to this farmer, such as having farm and weather experts on standby all the time." What is interesting about AgroInsight Pro is that it is so easy to use. The farmers do not need to be tech-savvies. The system displays intricate farming information in a straightforward manner that anyone can comprehend. The more unpredictable the weather, such instruments like AgroInsight Pro increasingly come into play. By linking new technology with applied agricultural expertise, we’re helping create a more prosperous future for food production and agriculture.

articleTitle: Delay and Power Optimization in 8-Bit ALU Using Reversible Logic
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Arithmetic Logic Units (ALUs) play a crucial role in digital processing, where optimizing power consumption and delay is essential for improved performance. The traditional low power 8-bit ALU on Reversible logic for nano processors [DRA-8] used the Dual Key Gate Pair (DKGP) gate. The proposed 8-bit ALU implements Haghparast and Navi Gate (HNG) and Control Output Gate (COG), leading to significant differences in architecture and performance. This ALU is evaluated based on power dissipation and delay, demonstrating a significant reduction in both compared to the DRA-8 design. The comparative analysis highlights trade-offs in circuit complexity, gate count, and garbage outputs, showcasing the efficiency of the optimized approach. The results confirm that the proposed Delay and Power optimization in 8-bit ALU using reversible logic (DPA-8) achieved superior power-delay performance, making it highly suitable for low-power, high-speed computing applications, particularly in nano processors and emerging reversible computing technologies.

articleTitle: Down Syndrome Detection and Classification Using Anfis Classification Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: An extra copy of chromosome 21 causes the genetic disorder known as Down syndrome (DS). Physical and mental difficulties result from this additional chromosome's impact on the body and brain's development. The proposed system contains preprocessing block, feature extraction block and classification block for DS detection process. The image enhancement has been performed on preprocessing stage, the features Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and Local Binary Pattern (LBP) are computed at feature extraction stage. The Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference (ANFIS) classifier has been used in classification stage to classify the fetus image into either normal or abnormal.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-Transformer Model with Attention-Based Decoding for Accurate Abdominal Organ Segmentation in Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Medical image segmentation is important in diagnosing diseases and planning treatments. Abdominal organ segmentation is difficult due to variations in shape, size, and position. Traditional methods struggle with unclear boundaries and overlapping structures. Deep learning models improve segmentation but often miss details or fail with complex shapes. A new deep learning model is designed to improve accuracy. It combines convolutional networks with transformers to capture both local and global features. The model extracts multi-scale features to preserve fine details. A transformer module processes global relationships between organs. An attention-based decoder refines segmentation masks to enhance boundary detection. The model is tested on medical datasets containing CT and MRI scans. It is compared with leading segmentation methods using standard metrics. The results show improved accuracy and better-defined organ boundaries. The Dice similarity score increases by 3% for liver segmentation and 5% for kidney segmentation. The model also reduces false positives and improves consistency in segmenting complex structures. This method addresses key challenges in abdominal organ segmentation. It captures fine details while understanding organ relationships. The improved accuracy makes it useful for clinical applications.

articleTitle: Automated Emergency Response System Using AI-Driven Patient Monitoring, Surveillance and Drug Delivery
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
