abstract: The following study discusses the development of a more intelligent and sophisticated healthcare system which is intended to provide better care to patients especially during critical conditions such as cardiac emergencies. The system seamlessly integrates several components such as on-site clinical supervision, identity management and unmanned therapeutic aid. The important element of the system is the incorporation of patient’s live recording with the employment of facial recognition of the visitors and machine-learning models. The most vital components in the response to any medical emergency is a live cam embedded with surveillance features and a mobile unit with the capability to autonomously disperse drugs. The hardware works in such a way that in the case of cardiac arrest or any other abnormal condition, the patient can automatically call the drug dispensing unit, and the unit autonomously locates the patient and delivers the drug. In simple terms the overall goal of the project was fragmentation of the patient verification and emergency drug administration tasks in order to make them easily manageable and efficient. The distinct vision claims to enhance access to emergency healthcare services by delivering real-time and effective medical assistance to patients irrespective of their location.

articleTitle: VLSI Implementation of Pipelined PE Systolic Array-Based 3x3 Matrix Multiplication for Deep Neural Network Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The demand for efficient, low-power, and high-speed deep neural network (DNN) accelerators has driven the need for specialized hardware architectures. This work presents the VLSI implementation of a DNN accelerator, building upon a prior project that utilized the systolic array architecture. We eliminate the conventional for-loop multiplication approach, leveraging the systolic array's data parallelism and pipelining to reduce clock cycle delays. The ReLU activation function is integrated into the systolic array to enable nonlinear transformations. Experimental results, obtained using 28nm technology using Synopsys Design Compiler, show that the systolic array with ReLU achieves a 19.9% power reduction and maintains a delay of 0.19 ps, with a marginal 0.69% area increase compared to the systolic array without ReLU. Pipelining further reduces clock cycle delays, enhancing real-time processing. This work demonstrates the potential of combining RNS, systolic arrays, and pipelining to design scalable, high-performance DNN accelerators for advanced tasks.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Gradient Boosting and Random Forest on Accuracy Improvement in Cardiovascular Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The aim of the study is to compare the performance of Random Forest and Gradient Boosting for enhancing cardiovascular risk prediction accuracy for early medical intervention. This study has two groups. Group 1 employs a Random Forest model trained on Framingham Heart Study and UCI Heart Disease data with features like age, gender, and blood pressure. Group 2 employs a Gradient Boosting model, validated against similar features, with performance indicators of accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score. Random Forest proved to be highly accurate with 84.5% accuracy at the 20th epoch, contrasted to Gradient Boosting that reached 88.0%. The models indicated improvement in prediction accuracy across 20 epochs. The Gradient Boosting model did better in accuracy (88.0%), precision (87.7%), recall 87.9% and f1-score at (87.8%) metrics than Random Forest. The Gradient Boosting mode did better across the board in cardiovascular disease prediction and is therefore a more reliable choice for detection. Gradient Boosting did better than Random Forest in accuracy (88.0%), precision (87.7%), and recall at 87.9% and F1-Score (87.8%) and is therefore more reliable for CVD prediction. Random Forest ranked lower on recall and accuracy and may be prone to missing cases of CVD. The study highlights the importance of choosing the right model in the detection early on.

articleTitle: Real-Time Stress Detection System with Integrated Facial Expression Analysis based Hybrid Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In order to address the growing concerns about stress, this project develops a state-of-the-art, multi-modal stress detection system that integrates emotion analysis with facial recognition. The system analyses facial pictures in real time by using a pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for stress estimate and OpenCV's Haar cascade for precise face identification. A k-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) algorithm is used to better examine emotional signals, improving stress assessment by combining emotional and physiological signs. Offering a cutting-edge method of mental health monitoring and intervention, this potent, real-time solution is perfect for a variety of applications, including personal well-being and business settings. The fusion model achieves the accuracy of 96% which is higher than the traditional methods for predicting the stress detection.

articleTitle: Innovative Metasurface-Assisted Star-Coupled Microstrip Antenna Array for Next-Generation Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The 20×16 mm wearable patch antenna is constructed on a Rogger R03210 substrate that is 1.2 mm thick. This antenna is 5.8 GHZ frequency working antenna with high gain of 8.5 dB. By utilizing a polyimide substrate, the device possesses a significant degree of flexibility, which requires both mechanical stability of device components and benefits to the users comfort for wearable devices. The compact and lightweight design makes its embedding into wearable platforms quite easily, thereby, meeting one of the critical space and weight constraints without much trade-off in terms of efficiency. The antenna’s effective radiation characteristics reduce interference and provide reliable wireless connectivity, making it perfect for the latest wearable and IoT technologies. Moreover, the design is excellent for operating in different environments, which enhances the usage of on-body and off- body communication. In conclusion, this patch antenna, which can be worn as part of a wearable device, is a great and efficient way to add wireless communication capability to existing wearable devices, ensuring that these devices can all connect without loss of performance or wearability.

articleTitle: Power efficient GSM-HMPAPM for Visible Light Ccommunications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Visible Light Communication (VLC) systems have emerged as a promising technology to support high-speed data transmission using light-emitting diodes (LED’s). Despite their potential, traditional modulation techniques face limitations in efficiency, spectral utilization, and compatibility with advanced VLC applications. This paper investigates the power and bandwidth requirements of Generalized Spatial Modulation – Multi Pulse Amplitude Position Modulation (GSM-MPAPM) and we propose a new algorithm to improve the same. By integrating a Hybrid algorithm for the Pulse position modulation in GSM-MPAPM we could achieve significant decrease in power consumption and bandwidth requirements. We propose a novel hybrid modulation technique called Generalized Spatial Modulation–Hybrid Multi Pulse Amplitude Position Modulation(GSM-HMPAPM). Theoretically, our modulation has shown an power consumption of 3.6075P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ook</inf> whereas for the same parameters the existing GSM-MPAPM requires 7.15P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ook</inf>. Practically, we achieved results proportional to theoretical values which will be discussed further.

articleTitle: Drug Recommendation System and Side Effects Based on Sentiment Analysis of Drug Reviews Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This study provides a medicine recommendation system that analyses the problems by applying machine learning and sentiment analysis approaches. Classification algorithms are used to predict sentiment and provide suitable medications based on these assessments. The powerful machine learning (ML) approaches can help to further improve this, which analyses unstructured data sources like user ratings, medical literature and patient reviews. For appropriate drug recommendations with no adverse effects, this study suggests a Priority Weight Allocation Model using User Ratings (PWAUR). Based on the results, which demonstrate 98% accuracy, the Gradient Boosting model using TF-IDF outperforms the other models. By effectively predicting and managing side effects, these systems can significantly improve patient outcomes. Index Terms: drug, sentiment analysis, TF-IDF, NLP, Stemming, Recommender System, Machine Learning, Gradient Boosting and BOW.

articleTitle: Sequential ResNet Framework for Lung Cancer Classification: A Comparative Analysis of Bottom-Up and Top-Down Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Lung cancer detection in histopathological images is pivotal in timely and accurate diagnosis, directly influencing treatment outcomes and patient survival rates. This research paper presents an automated detection and classification system utilizing ResNet architectures. Initially, individual evaluations of ResNet-50, ResNet-101, and ResNet-152 are conducted. Subsequently, a sequential ResNet framework is developed to assess the combined performance of these architectures. In this framework, both top-down (ResNet-152 ➔ ResNet-101 ➔ ResNet-50) and bottom-up (ResNet-50 ➔ ResNet-101 ➔ ResNet152) approaches are employed for classification tasks. The effectiveness of the framework is measured using standard assessment metrics, including Accuracy, G-Mean, F1-score, Precision, Recall, and ROC curves for each architecture. The results signifies that the bottom-up approach achieves the outstanding performance in accuracy of 93.28% with an AUC value of 0.9800, indicating excellent classification performance and minimal false positives.

articleTitle: A Novel CNN based Classification of Anterior Talofibular Ligament in T2 Axial Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Plantar flexion and foot inversion contribute to about 70% of lateral ankle sprains, with anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) experiencing the most in jury in these situations. For patients to treat and heal from ATFL injuries, a swift and accurate diagnosis is essential. However, radiologists’ traditional techniques of interpreting Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRIs) can be labor-intensive and vulnerable to human error. To try to overcome these challenges, this research developed an advanced Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model that automatically identifies ATFL MRI scans as either abnormal or normal. The Image processing method comprises an extensive setup process that includes augmentation, greyscale images transformation, applying Gaussian blur to minimize noise, and cropping using contour recognition. Images are scaled and normalized after preprocessing and then sent into CNN for training. When measured using many metrics, including precision, recall, and F1 score, the CNN model performed very well, achieving a diagnostic accuracy of 94.45%. This indicates that the CNN model is effective in distinguishing between normal and abnormal ATFL conditions. This prominent level of accuracy not only promises to significantly reduce the diagnostic workload for radiologists but also enhances the speed and reliability of the diagnostic process. The objective is to boost the application of this technology in clinical settings, which could result in better outcomes for patients, more effective diagnostic processes, improved medical imaging, and enhanced healthcare delivery in general. Future work will try to grow the dataset’s capacity to include a more diverse range of images and explore its potential application to the diagnosis of other ligament injuries.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of an Efficient Memristor Based Multiplier Using Hybird Logic
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The scalability and power inefficiency concerns related to conventional CMOS technology are taken up in this work, which improves the design for high-performance memristor-based digital circuits. This research proposes alternative arithmetic circuit implementations, including half adders, full adders, 2-bit multipliers, and 3-bit multipliers, using the HP memristor's nanosecond-scale switching speeds, non-volatility, and CMOS compatibility. These circuits, containing experimentally verified HP memristor models with exact current-voltage (I-V) characteristics, were developed and simulated using MATLAB and LTspice. Considering the memristor's sudden resistive switching and low-energy state transitions, the results show significant increases in power efficiency (up to 45% reduction) and operational speed (30% faster switching) compared to CMOS equivalents. The HP memristor's more accurate Ron/Roff ratios and endurance are highlighted in a comparative analysis, demonstrating its suitability for hybrid memristor-CMOS designs [1]. Stable hysteresis curves are shown by transient simulations under different bias conditions and dielectric thicknesses, and resilience against process variations and thermal impacts is confirmed. This study gives vital insights into hybrid system optimization by bridging the gap between theoretical models and real-world implementation with the addition of experimental I-V data from constructed HP memristors. The outcomes depend on the groundwork for memory systems and flexible, energy-efficient arithmetic logic units (ALUs), with implications for beyond-CMOS applications and neuromorphic computing.

articleTitle: Soil Texture Prediction: Advances in Remote Sensing, Image Analysis, and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Soil texture is critical in soil behavior regulation since it controls its physical and chemical biological properties. The properties determine plant development, water absorption capabilities, and natural nutrient cycles. The accuracy of hydrometer and pipette methods remains authentic, but their implementation proves to be unscalable due to expensive equipment requirements, high complexity, and lengthy processing times. Soil texture predictions became feasible because of advancements in remote sensing, digital image processing, and machine learning (ML) technology, which allow both high-scale prediction and low-cost and fast execution. An analysis examines how satellite information merges with proximal sensing through applicable ML models such as RF, SVM, CNNs, and hybrid deep learning techniques for conducting soil texture predictions. The paper evaluates regional and global examples with Land Use/Cover Area Frame Survey (LUCAS) datasets and Soil Grids and Indian Soil Health Card (ISRIC) schemes while discussing the benefits of smartphone-based systems. The article presents technical comparisons before exploring obstacles and prospective developments, including integrating IoT and AI-based frameworks.The review shows how new methods help sustainable agriculture, precision farming, and environmental protection through precise big-scale mapping of soil textures that support decision-making.

articleTitle: Design and Comparison of Hybrid Optimization controllers for Artificial Respiration System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Artificial ventilation is vital for managing respiratory disorders, especially sustaining oxygen levels in severe patients. A motor-driven respiratory system with a piston mechanism must effectively manage volume to ensure smooth respiration. This study optimizes controller parameters using hybrid methodologies to create an automated breathing system. Two PID controllers—Hybrid Fminimax-Simulated Annealing and Hybrid Fmincon-Genetic Algorithm—were used with ISE, IAE, and ITAE as objectives. A comparative investigation reveals that the Hybrid Fmincon-Genetic Algorithm-based PID controller optimized with ITAE has the highest stability and performance.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enhanced Zero-Trust Architecture for Secure Key Management in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) require secure key management to prevent unauthorized access. Traditional methods rely on centralized authentication, which increases key compromise risks. These methods also fail to provide continuous verification and adaptive trust evaluation. A secure and scalable approach is needed to protect cryptographic keys and improve authentication. This research proposes a Blockchain-Enhanced Zero-Trust Architecture (BE-ZTA) for secure key management in WSNs. The zero-trust model enforces strict authentication and continuous monitoring of all network nodes. The blockchain ledger stores cryptographic keys securely, preventing tampering and unauthorized modifications. Smart contracts automate key updates and revocation, ensuring that compromised keys are immediately replaced. The proposed method solves key security problems by eliminating central points of failure and preventing unauthorized access. The zero-trust model continuously evaluates node behavior and assigns dynamic trust scores. The blockchain ledger ensures tamper-proof key storage and real-time verification. Smart contracts provide automated and decentralized key management, reducing security risks. Experimental results confirm that the proposed method improves authentication accuracy to 97.2%. The key compromise rate is reduced by 45%, ensuring better security. The model reduces network latency to 2.1 milliseconds, improving efficiency. Attack detection efficiency exceeds 95%, preventing key compromise, MITM, and Sybil attacks.

articleTitle: Power-Efficient Design of Full Adder Using XOR-XNOR Logic and Input-Controlled Leakage Restrainer Transistors in 14nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The reason for the rising importance of power efficiency in digital arithmetic circuits is the use of submicron CMOS technologies. This paper presents a new full adder design that uses XOR-XNOR logic with ICLRT technology and is fabricated using a 14nm CMOS process. It employs the ICLRT mechanism for dynamic control over leakage currents, thus minimizing power dissipation and enhancing performance metrics compared to other full adder designs.A detailed analysis of the proposed design shows significant reductions in leakage power and power-delay product, making it suitable for low-power and high- performance applications. The XOR- XNOR logic provides full-swing outputs, ensuring signal integrity while being scalable to wide word-length architectures.The full adder design has been simulated using advanced circuit design tools under process, voltage, and temperature variations to validate its robustness and reliability. The proposed approach demonstrates a comparative improvement in average power consumption, propagation delay, and PDP while remaining compatible with advanced requirements for VLSI integration. These results highlight the efficiency of this XOR-XNOR logic-based full adder design as a superior alternative for energy-efficient digital systems.

articleTitle: Broken Stick Regressive Convolution Neural Learning based Blood Group Detection with Fingerprint Images
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Fingerprints are the accurate method for identifying an individual. Blood group detection is an essential medical diagnostic for guaranteeing the compatibility and prenatal care. Different researchers carried out their research on blood group detection with fingerprint images. But accuracy level was not improved and time consumption was not reduced by existing methods. In order to address these issues, a new deep learning model called Broken Stick Regressive Convolution Neural Learning (BSRCNL) Method is introduced. The main objective of BSRCNL method is to perform efficient blood group detection with fingerprint images to enhance accessibility, efficiency and ease of blood type identification.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Wearable for Remote Healthcare Monitoring to Manage Stress
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Stress is a pervasive problem plaguing modern society, impacting people of all ages, genders, origins, and workplace settings. This paper discussed the psychological and physiological consequences of stress, particularly as it relates to managing the environmental pressures of work, family, and acute life events. Chronic stress impacts people in countless ways, creating substantial risks to mental, physical health, and job performance. The research underlines the importance of comprehending stress at various levels in the context of the modern world, pointing to its widespread, prolonged, and complicated nature. In order to deal with this problem, a new Internet of Things (IoT) solution has been created that combines several sensors for holistic stress monitoring. This solution provides 80% accuracy in detecting stress, which is higher than available solutions. Through the use of IoT technology, the suggested strategy provides more improved stress management functions, allowing individuals, groups, and organizations to further defend themselves against stress's destructive effects in their lives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Safety Prediction in Accident-prone Zones using Gradient Boosting Machines
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The aim of this study is to improve safety prediction in accident hotspots through the use of gradient boosting machines (GBM) and comparing their performance with K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). It measures predictive accuracy, validity, and overall performance in the analysis of accident data. Materials and methods: Group 1applies KNN for safety prediction using 26 samples, measured on 90.4% accuracy, 88.6% recall precision, and F1-score. Group 2 applies GBM for accident risk estimation using 26 samples, measured on the same performance metrics accuracy of 97.5%, a recall of 96.8%. Results: Accuracy for GBM was between 85.4% and 96.7% with a high of 92.5% at a level of significance of 0.0048, while KNN varied between 72.3% and 89.1%. Conclusion: GBM's better feature selection and ensemble learning make it a superior model for real-time estimation of accident risk.

articleTitle: Hybrid FrFT-HS Framework for High-Accuracy Lung Cancer Classification from Gene Expression Data
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Lung cancer classification from microarray gene expression data presents a significant challenge due to high dimensionality and redundant features. This study employs the Fast Fractional Fourier Transform (FFrFT) for dimensionality reduction, followed by Harmonic Search (HS) for optimal feature selection. Various classifiers, including Bayesian Linear Discriminant Classifier (BLDC), Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Naive Bayesian Classifier (NBC), Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) with Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel, were evaluated for classification performance. Experimental results show that SVM (RBF) attained an impressive accuracy of 91.16%. This outstanding performance underscores the significant impact of proposed dimensionality reduction and feature selection pipeline in enhancing classification performance.

Author Keywords: Lung cancer classification Micro array gene data

articleTitle: CredShield: Decentralized AI for Secure and Adaptive Credit Risk Management
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The amount of credit card default prediction is large because banks and financial institutions are searching for a method to predict cards that can be chosen according to the borrower’s credibility. This work predicts how people will pay for credit with transactional and demographic data and runs a few models of machine learning, i.e. logistic regression, random forest, and neural network. Because data can be partitioned to understand and enhance the likelihood of accurate prediction success, KMeans is combined with DBSCAN clustering to improve the accuracy of prediction as the performance of data depends on the input data, which is less than the performance of defined DBSCAN. The results of the proposed method of this UCI machine learning repository dataset were 99.32% compared to traditional models that were 82.8% and 83.5%, respectively. One is the need to do data normalization, and the other is to select appropriate methods for multifold validation to get maximum performance. Ultimately, this solid analytical system aids in finer credit risk analysis, inhibits inclusion of default, and so ends up with heart-wrenching and lucrative loan approvals.

articleTitle: Design of Modified Bacterial Foraging Algorithm (MBFA) FIR Filter for Signal Processing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters are widely used in digital signal processing (DSP) software, and optimization is required for better performance, faster computation, and flexibility. This paper describes the Modified Bacterial Foraging Algorithm (MBFA) to optimize the FIR filter coefficients that addresses major concerns in power usage, resource utilization, and rate of processing. The new design integrates Common Subexpression Elimination (CSE) and Canonical Signed Digit (CSD) methods for the elimination of redundant computation, decreasing hardware complexity, and improving energy efficiency. The architecture minimizes redundant multiplications and leverages best coefficient values to reduce power consumption and area significantly without sacrificing accuracy. The FIR filter is designed in Xilinx Vivado, and performance is measured in terms of important parameters like power consumption, delay, and resource utilization. Relative comparison with traditional optimization methods confirms the dominance of the MBFA-based FIR filter in the achievement of an optimal trade-off between performance and computational complexity. The results confirm MBFA as a strong and powerful optimization framework for improving the overall efficiency of FIR filter design. This study contributes to the design of low-power and high-speed DSP systems and is thus relevant in high-performance applications that require real-time processing

articleTitle: Optimized QCA SRAM for Efficient MAC Operations in AI Workloads
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a complete Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) cell using Quantum-dot Cellular Automata (QCA) technology. The proposed SRAM is designed to store critical data required for Machine Learning (ML) algorithm training, with a focus on enhancing data transfer rates, particularly in Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) operations. We have successfully implemented and tested the Quantum-dot inverted cell, demonstrating its functionality and potential for acceleration. Furthermore, the implementation of a QCA buffer, exhibiting 90% similarity to conventional buffers, confirms the reliability and scalability of our design for data storage processes. Building upon these foundational components, we have successfully realized the complete QCA-based SRAM architecture. The implemented SRAM demonstrates effective data storage and retrieval, offering a promising solution for efficient data storage and processing in AI hardware systems. This work validates the feasibility and benefits of QCA-based SRAM for enhancing performance in demanding AI applications.

articleTitle: Explainable AI in Stroke Treatment and Rehabilitation Monitoring: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence systems have produced remarkable outcomes during the last ten years, particularly in computer vision and natural language processing. Explainable AI (EXAI) is a broad field that includes several techniques aimed at providing insights into a model's internal operations, elucidating outputs, or improving the system's overall interpretability for end users, including human decision-makers. A crucial concept in artificial intelligence that aims to improve the transparency and interpretability of intricate models of machine learning is EXAI. Unlike conventional "black-box" algorithms, EXAI aims to create models that can offer concise, intelligible justifications for their choices. As a result, stakeholders are more equipped to understand and assess the reasoning behind AI-driven conclusions, which encourages accountability and the moral application of AI. Particularly in areas where decision-making insights are critical, EXAI is indispensable. In response to the growing complexity of neural networks, EXAI has progressed from conventional machine learning to deep learning. This article reviews the recent advancements of EXAI in stroke treatment as well as its rehabilitation monitoring.

articleTitle: Sonar-Based Rock and Mine Detection for Enhancing Efficiency in Underwater Exploration and Security
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging) is one of the critical techniques used for detection and location of underwater objects. Distinguishing harmless objects such as rocks from hazardous threats like mines is vital for successful naval operations and maritime security. This article discusses how the introduction of machine learning techniques will bring about a difference in this process. The results have shown that 80-90% accuracy could be achieved in the process using an appropriately designed machine learning model. The improved classification of underwater objects is, no doubt the most significant benefit of incorporating machine learning into the SONAR technology, which ensures the process both safer and efficient. Machine learning does not directly involve humans; hence, unlike traditional methods, it reduces risks to operators.Four different machine learning algorithms were used, namely Logistic Regression, K- Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM). The model performance metrics analysis was done to ensure a detailed comparison of which algorithm is best. Besides proving the supremacy of machine learning, this comparative study provides an accurate performance evaluation to ensure that the best model is selected for practical applications. The integration of multiple algorithms underscores the adaptability and robustness of machine learning, highlighting its potential to enhance SONAR technology for safer and more efficient maritime operations.

articleTitle: Neural Sequence Modelling for Spam Classification via Bidirectional LSTM and Hierarchical Neural Networks: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Spam messages are a major problem in digital communication. They are a breach of privacy, facilitate financial fraud and result in unnecessary clutter in one’s inbox. Most traditional methods for spam filtering are based on the older machine learning approaches. Such approaches rely on hand-crafted features which are inadequate to detect novel and progressively complex varieties of spam. As the spam messages become more sophisticated and sophisticated, we clearly require better detection algorithms. It must be able to detect small details in the text and understand the context of the messages in order to identify and filter out the spam effectively.In this paper a deep learning architecture for accurate classification of spam using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) networks is introduced. The proposed method tokenizes, uses embedding layers and sequence modeling to effectively analyze SMS texts in order to distinguish between spam and non spam contents. A publicly available dataset of 5,574 SMS messages was used in this study, which included 4,827 non-spam messages and 747 spam messages. To this end, the dataset was first preprocessed through text normalization, stop word removal, and padding to ensure that the input sequences were of consistent length. In order to prevent overfitting, the model was trained with an optimum learning rate, an appropriate sample size, and dropout regularization procedures. The best performing model was the BiLSTM model which was able to process sequences in both directions and achieved an accuracy of 97.3%, precision of 95.6%, recall of 96.1% and an F1-score of 95.8%. The high recall score indicates that the model is able to correctly identify spam without many false negatives which is a critical component of an effective spam detection system. The study compares the accuracy of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks with usual classifiers such as SVM, Naïve Bayes, and Random Forest. The former technique shows better performance than traditional models in correctly identifying sequential links within text messages. Although the results are promising, there are still major issues to be addressed, such as dealing with skewed datasets and improving processing efficiency. Attention mechanisms to better understand context and respond to the new spam methods. This paper demonstrates show deep learning can be applied to develop a more reliable and automated spam detection thereby enhancing security and privacy.

articleTitle: Smart IoT based Monitoring System for Autism Patients
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: There have been different wireless technologies, and several recent trends have produced patient tracking systems to monitor the patient’s performance. Along with performance tracking, patient movement tracking is also necessary as it concerns safety measures. In such cases, tracking helps caretakers know the whereabouts of patients. The main aim of this proposed scheme is to keep track of the patients, and if any unusual activity is detected, caretakers are immediately informed through an alarm. Additionally, a panic switch is integrated into the system, allowing patients to send an emergency alert to their caretakers with a single press in case of distress. With this project, caretakers can easily determine their patient’s location within the perimeter. The whole project consists of two units: the first is the school unit, where a BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) device is worn like a watch, and the second is the bus unit, where a mobile module with an app is placed. With the help of an Android application, all patient details are sent to their caretakers in real time.

articleTitle: Channel Characterization of Ultra Massive MIMO Systems Utilizing Millimeter Waves For 6G Vehicular Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The characteristics of ultra-massive MIMO (UM-MIMO) systems that apply millimeter waves for 6G vehicular communication functions is evaluated in this work. This paper investigates path gain and root mean square delay spread together with path loss exponent across an indoor office space at 60 GHz through Wireless InSite (WI) 3D modeling in combination with Matlab-based ray tracing simulation techniques. The research reveals path gain values show substantial changes as a result of multipath propagation together with material properties and antenna configurations which affect signal behavior based on transmitter placement within the environment. With RMS delay spread analysis high-gain antennas prove vital in reducing the extent of channel dispersion. The research proved coverage predictions by combining statistical models and ray-tracing simulations which matched analytical results closely. The study generates essential knowledge to improve UM-MIMO deployment in future vehicular networks because it advances network functionality while strengthening complex communication stability.

articleTitle: An Experimental Analysis of Brain Tumor Detection Using Contemporize CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: A growth of brain tumor or abnormal cells leads to the cancerous. Cells in a brain tumor proliferate rapidly and indefinitely, and the tumor's pace of growth is uncontrollable. Deep learning has been proposed as a potential solution to the challenges of diagnosing and treating brain cancer. Deep learning and machine learning algorithms provide a quicker prediction of a brain tumor, and a better degree of accuracy facilitates patient care. The goal of this study was to develop a contemporize convolutional neural network (CNN) model framework and provide training and accuracy prediction parameters. Our suggested technique was tested on a dataset for brain tumor diagnosis using MRI images showing 150 tumors. In the testing data, the algorithm achieved remarkable accuracy of 94%, validation accuracy of 92.34%, and test accuracy of 94.5%, surpassing current conventional methods for brain cancer detection.

articleTitle: DDoS Attack Classification Using Adaptive Multiphase ensemble with Temporal Reinforcement
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In the era of rapid digital change, DDoS attacks present a major challenge to network security by disrupting the availability of critical services. Traditional detection methods often struggle with high false-positive rates and delayed response times due to the evolving nature of attack patterns. This paper proposes AMPETR++ (Adaptive Multi-Phase Ensemble with Temporal Reinforcement), a novel hybrid framework for DDoS attack detection and classification using machine learning techniques. The AMPETR++ model integrates three core phases: Statistical Analysis, Frequency-Based Feature Extraction, and Behavioral Analysis, to extract comprehensive features from the network traffic dataset. The model combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM neural networks with adaptive weight optimization to improve detection accuracy. Additionally, the Temporal Reinforcement Learning Mechanism filters predictions based on past observations, enhancing the model's performance over time. The proposed framework demonstrates superior performance compared to other models, achieving high accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score on benchmark datasets. The results highlight the model’s ability to dynamically adapt to varying attack patterns, making it a promising approach for real-time DDoS attack detection and prediction in cybersecurity systems.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of Perovskite-Based Solar Cells and Photodetectors with the Hybrid Heterostructure of SnO2/CH3NH3PbI3/NiO Thin films
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have shown high optical absorption and provide high conversion efficiency with stable performance. The use of this perovskite as the active layer of photodetectors shows improved recognition and stability by converting light radiation impulses into electrical signals, thereby finding applications in scientific research, as well as military and civic domains. In this work, we model the SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/NiO structure using SCAPS-1D software. A comprehensive analysis was performed for important SC parameters such as power conversion efficiency (PCE), fill factor (FF), open circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>), short circuit current (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>), and external quantum efficiency (EQE) by taking into account layer thickness and defect density. The External Quantum Efficiency can be observed respectively under an illumination of white 400-800.spe.

articleTitle: 4x2 Microstrip Patch Array Antenna for 5G Mid-Band Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In this paper, a microstrip patch antenna is designed for array-based 5G Mid-Band applications. The antenna is designed to work at Sub-6 GHz Communication in the frequency range of 4.34 to 5.1 GHz, maximizing communication speed, minimizing latency, and improving system performance. The suggested design is a rectangular microstrip patch of size 27.8 mm × 26.9 mm, with four slots (4.06 mm x 3 mm each) for gain improvement. By arranging the antenna in an array of 4 x 2, the gain is enhanced to 9.19 dBi. Simulations were performed using Keysight ADS software. First, a square patch antenna with a 26.9 mm size was tried, and it had a 2.24 dBi gain. When it was shaped into a rectangular patch with slots, its gain was increased to 3.78 dBi. The antenna is constructed over an FR-4 substrate (dielectric constant: 4.4) of 1.6 mm thickness and with an interface thickness of 1 mm. The simulated and experimental results match well, and this verifies the correctness of the design. In comparison to conventional antennas, this design has greater gain and a superior reflection coefficient, thus making it a better option for practical use.

articleTitle: Bio Cognitive Mesh: Harnessing Swarm Intelligence for Self-Organizing AI at the Network Edge
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Unprecedented challenges of growing edge computing and the Internet of Things (IoT) have created the need of the hour to change the architecture of unchanging centralized AI [1], [2]. In this paper, we describe a framework for deploying decentralized artificial intelligence using swarm intelligence in edge computing networks such that all intelligence algorithms can be executed concurrently through swarm intelligence. Currently, most traditional AI deployment requires heavy and centralized reliance on the cloud infrastructure, leading to data transmission bottlenecks, higher latency, and privacy concerns [3], [4]. We use bio-inspired swarm algorithms to distribute computational intelligence across edge devices in a fashion whose computational intelligence is collectively made without central control [5], [6]. We demonstrate consistent improvements in smart city infrastructure, autonomous vehicle testbeds, and IoT networks: reducing latency by 78x, decreasing bandwidth consumption by 83x, and securing system resilience while maintaining model accuracy. This research contributes to the edge AI field by presenting a scalable and resilient architecture for distributed intelligence on constrained resources [7], [8].

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Early Detection And Monitoring Of Respiratory Disorder Using PCO2 Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Respiratory disorders like Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), asthma, and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) pose significant health risks worldwide. This study presents a machine learning-driven framework for early detection and monitoring of these conditions using Partial Pressure of Carbon Dioxide (PCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) analysis. The methodology employs the Chi<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Probability Density Function (Chi<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> PDF) and Cuckoo Search (CS) model for dimensionality reduction. Harmonic Search (HS) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) are utilized for optimized feature selection. Models such as Nonlinear Regression (NLR), Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Linear Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine with Radial Basis Function (SVM-RBF), and Logistic Regression (LoR) are used for disorder detection. The proposed system achieved an accuracy of 95.71. This approach offers a non-invasive, cost-effective solution to enhance respiratory healthcare and improve patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Predictive Plant Irrigation Management System Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Precision farming makes use of cutting-edge technology such as automation, machine learning (ML), and the internet of things (IoT) to improve agricultural productivity by making data-driven decisions. Based on real-time environmental and soil sensor data, this study proposes an automated irrigation categorization system that makes use of IoT and machine learning to forecast crop irrigation needs. The system integrates Raspberry Pi, Arduino, and IoT sensors, enabling automated decision-making after being trained on a dataset sourced from Kaggle. Random Forest Classifier (RFC) had the highest accuracy, with 98.02% and the least root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.14, according to a comparison of machine learning models, including RFC, Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC), and XGBoost. The findings show that ensemble learning approaches increase classification precision, guaranteeing ideal soil moisture content and effective water allocation. The suggested method provides a scalable and effective way to maximize crop productivity, reduce water waste, and optimize irrigation. In the future, the proposed system helps in irrigation management and support resource-efficient and sustainable precision agriculture, future developments will investigate weather forecasting models and deep learning approaches.

articleTitle: Improving Software Quality in Software Development using Random Forest Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In an era where software drives critical systems across industries, ensuring high-quality software before deployment is essential to enhance reliability, security, efficiency, and user satisfaction while minimizing risks, costs, and failures. One effective approach is defect management that prevent failures and enhance overall system performance. Datasets used for defect prediction suffer from class imbalance. Learning from imbalanced data and hyperparameter values of machine learning (ML) algorithms has affected the performance of prediction models that they generate. In this paper, we used JM1, one of the dataset from NASA promise dataset repository which suffer from class imbalance problem that leads to inaccurate classification and prediction. This research aims to improve the prediction of Random Forest (RF) classifier by addressing data imbalance. Specifically, it employs a hybrid approach combining Nearmiss undersampling and SMOTE oversampling to create a balanced dataset. The study then evaluates and compares F1-score of the enhanced RF model against Decision Tree (DT) and Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost) classifiers. The experimental findings proved that Random Forest (RF) was the most effective classifier for detecting defects.

articleTitle: ANFIS-Based PWM Control for Electric Vehicle Speed Regulation Using an Intelligent ECU with ARM Processor
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The main aim of this investigation is to optimize speed stability under dynamic load conditions, minimize energy usage, improve response time, and increase vehicle safety by enhanced PWM signal. The flaws of the traditional ECU will be solved with a high-performance intelligent ECU which comprises the ARM Processor with supporting Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System algorithms. In order to optimize motor performance by the design and development of an intelligent and energy-efficient electronic control unit (ECU). The trained Neuro fuzzy inference model will provide the efficient PWM pulses according to the accelerator pedal signal of the EV by using bare metal coding. This proposed method produced a well enhanced output of 91.2% energy efficiency, Speed Regulation Accuracy 98.7 % also error will be minimized by 1.1% from 3.2% using Embedded Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System in STM32 Controller. This proposed system enhances electric vehicles speed optimization and energy efficiency. The ANFIS algorithm uses the greater number of iteration and signal sampling which provides the optimized output and minimizing errors to enhance the promotion of sustainable EV technology development.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Acute Appendicitis from Contrast-enhanced CT Scans using Generative Adversarial Networks for Augmented Classification in Acute Abdomen Cases
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The research introduces an innovative method to detect acute appendicitis by uniting symptom-based forecasting with state-of-the-art image analysis techniques. The system employs an FNN for syndrome evaluation which interacts with a 3D ResNet model for analyzing CT scan contrast images with the objective to enhance diagnostic speed while increasing accuracy. Users supply patient symptoms to an FNN model that calculates appendicitis risk probabilities. User needs to upload CT scan files when the system detects probabilities exceeding the designated threshold. The system uses 3D ResNet to examine the uploaded images. Users benefit from the MERN stack-based website because it delivers an intuitive experience for both symptom entry and CT scan file upload capabilities. The machine learning models that run for real-time predictions operate on FastAPI infrastructure. This two-level diagnostic process quickly delivers precise appendicitis diagnosis that assists health care professionals in their medical choices. A forthcoming enhancement plan includes the addition of components for patient management as well as appointment scheduling while adding extra predictive models to enhance system strength.

articleTitle: Integrating Explainability into RNNs for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Such advancement of deep learning models, especially in the recurrent neural networks in the medical diagnostics had been very potent to predict the diagnoses of several diseases, including the Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), though such dark-box nature of RNN also hampers in terms of its model interpretability, that is indispensable for the clinical area. A proposed study is the integration of newly devised explainability techniques, such as attention mechanisms, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), and Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP), with RNNs to predict ALS diagnosis. On the dataset of 1,500 patient records suffering from ALS, it was observed that the model increased its transparency to 25%, with 85% accuracy in prediction and 90% user satisfaction in the clinical scenario. This conclusion opens the way for the potential of explainable RNNs in the improvement of ALS diagnosis and decision-making.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for High-Frequency Bitcoin Trading and Market Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The large price changes in Bitcoin have led to increased interest in predicting its future prices. This study uses a Deep learning approach to forecast Bitcoin values based on past data and technical indicators. Several models, including LSTM and Gradient Boosting, are used to find patterns in Bitcoin's price trends. Results show that the LSTM model reaches an accuracy of 98%. It also achieves a 97% accuracy rate for daily price predictions using logistic regression and linear discriminant analysis methods. The use of LSTM for predicting Bitcoin prices over time is more effective than traditional methods, especially regarding the importance of sample size in Deep learning. The analysis looks at Bitcoin price charts to project future changes, primarily through time series analysis that utilizes historical data. Deep learning algorithms are applied to identify complex patterns in Bitcoin pricing data. The dataset for these predictions is from KAGGLE, covering eight years from 2014 to 2022, which aids in developing more accurate forecasting techniques.

Author Keywords: Deep Learning Applications in Cryptocurrency and Bitcoin

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Techniques for Early Diagnosis of Parkinson’s Disease: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This evaluation article reviews the brand new reputation of applications to early Parkinson's disease (PD) analysis. PD is shown to have an effect on around 1% of individuals over the age of 60, the percentage growing with age. Early Parkinson's disease analysis is vital to improved outcomes and slowed disease progression. The main objective of the paper is to examine Parkinson's disorder at the preliminary stage, the usage of various gadgets, and knowledge of tools. From the evaluation of diverse methodologies, algorithms, and information sets, we give an explanation for how AI techniques have revolutionized the early prognosis of PD. This summarizes findings of the latest research studies comparing numerous system studying techniques like deep learning, support vector machines, and random forests. Findings indicate that device-based getting to know are quite accurate for the identification of early PD using a range of biomarkers, with fulfillment in evaluating voice styles, gait parameters, and neuroimaging features. This paper explores the detailed demanding situations and barriers in present methodologies and promising future directions.

articleTitle: A Software-Defined Zero Trust Framework for Secure Access Control and Microsegmentation using SDN and SDP
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In the growing world of network security, traditional defense models like firewall, IPS/IDS are not enough to be used against modern cyber threats. To handle this we have introduced a solution that can adapt to the current network trends. This paper presents a approach, Software-Defined Zero Trust Framework that combines Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and Software-Defined Perimeter (SDP) to provide us with strict access control and microsegmentation. The proposed framework combines SDN controllers with SDP mechanisms to manage network access, making sure that only the users and devices which are verified are allowed before establishing any connections. Unlike traditional approaches, our model improvises the security by applying fine-grained segmentation, least-privilege access, and password policy enforcement, effectively reducing the attack surface and also, we demonstrate the framework’s implementation and evaluate its effectiveness in securing network communications. The outcomes show that using this approach help us strengthen the security of the overall network by reducing lateral movement threats which prevents attackers from moving within and across the network through segmentation using flow rules and maintain traffic control within the network while not affecting the network speed and strict access control. This paper is proposed as contribution to the ongoing research for Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) by providing a lightweight, scalable, and resource-efficient security model suitable for modern cloud and enterprise environments.

articleTitle: Application of Advanced Data Mining and Computer Vision Techniques in License Plate Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: As urbanization is expanding rapidly and vehicular traffic is on the rise, efficient and automated vehicle identification is a must. Smart transportation, safety monitoring, & police work all heavily rely on Automatic License Plate Detection (ALPD). Traditional heuristic-based image processing techniques are incapable of handling environmental variations; Artificial intelligence (AI) & machine vision solutions are therefore used. YOLO, Faster R-CNN, and SSD are some of the most effective CNN-based and object identification algorithms that demonstrate cutting-edge accuracy in license plate recognition. The paper studies the usage of deep learning algorithms with prepossessing and advanced localization methods for ALPDs' optical character recognition (OCR) and character segmentation. The research also studies integrating ALPD with edge computing and IoTs to develop real-time smart traffic solutions. It also examines machine learning techniques, deep learning innovations, and conventional methods, emphasizing how well various models perform in comparison in terms of accuracy, computational efficiency, and real-time processing power. By employing cutting-edge designs, this study seeks to increase the scalability and resilience of license plate recognition systems, which will support future urban development, security applications, as intelligent transportation management.

articleTitle: Dynamic Music Composition System Using LSTM and Transformer Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper introduces a music composition system using AI democratizing creative expression by leveraging deep learning technologies. By utilizing LSTM and Transformer neural networks trained on MIDI datasets, our system produces unique compositions from user input. The architecture employs a Streamlit frontend, Flask/FastAPI backend, and sophisticated music processing pipeline. Users describe mood, genre, tempo, and instrumentation using an easy-to-use interface, with real-time-generated compositions. Feature extraction operations transform MIDI into learnable representations, and Qdrant vector storage facilitates similarity-based inspiration. Real-time adaptation improves compositions recursively based on user feedback. Experimental benchmarking with 85 subjects showed 87% satisfaction with mood representation and 92% accuracy with genre classification, with average generation times of 3.8 seconds for 30-second compositions. This work promotes computational creativity through the integration of advanced AI models with user-friendly interfaces, changing the way non-musicians interact with music composition without sacrificing theoretical integrity.

articleTitle: Optimizing Chronic Kidney Disease Prediction Through Advanced Data Imputation and Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a slowly worsening disease that can hurt the patients in large numbers from all over the world. The article employs a mixed machine learning technique that unites clustering and supervised learning in order to detect CKD. The data has several checks applied, namely, typographical errors fixed, missing value estimation will be done using K-Nearest Neighbors(KNN) and feature optimization. The unsupervised techniques such as clustering will be adopted with that of the prediction of the hidden patterns that are not directly observable which are the most difficult models for a human to come up with. Moreover, the predictive models are re-trained on the enhanced dataset in order to offer a highly efficient CKD classification test. The study has shown that the clustering analysis makes it possible for the interpretation of high-risk cohorts to be conducted while giving inputs in identifying the progression of the disease. The phase of predictive modeling involves the use of different machine learning algorithms to evaluate the functionalities to ensure the correct classification. The merger of clustering with predictive analytics offers a new way for finding the CKD diagnosis and early detection strategies. The research points out the importance of data-driven methods in health care and shows how a preprocessing pipeline is built up with advanced technologies that could generate almost exact predictions. They also lead to the capability of AI-based processes where these tools can assist medical personnel in the diagnosis of early CKD and intervention. The pathway that future scientific research might follow refers to the specific niche of deep learning and the wider use of datasets which would both bring up the advantage of generalizability.

articleTitle: Advancing Eye Disease and Glaucoma Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Survey of Deep Learning, Machine Learning, and Hybrid Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Glaucoma stands as a serious global health issue among eye diseases because the condition leads to permanent blindness when proper diagnosis and treatment are not made in sufficient time. The detection and classification capabilities for these conditions have been significantly improved by recent developments in computational techniques that combine deep learning and traditional machine learning and hybrid models alongside clinical assessments. The survey explores 54 research studies regarding eye disease diagnosis which the authors divide into four distinct sections. Deep learning algorithms particularly CNN variants achieved outstanding success (93.5%) when used for retinal image segmentation together with disease classification tasks. Hybrid models equipped with machine learning and deep learning capabilities reached the maximum accuracy level at 95% for diagnosing diseases. SVMs and other traditional machine learning algorithms delivered accurate results for structured datasets through their performance while medical evaluations helped identify disease trajectories and disease elements. The study presents a thorough overview of the advantages along with drawbacks and potential applications for these analysis techniques in detecting and treating glaucoma along with other eye conditions.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Methodology to Energy Administration and Cost Reduction approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: To address the challenges of integrating clean power resources and evolving microgrid technologies, new energy control methods are essential. This work introduces Fuzzy Logic-Based Particle Swarm Optimization (FLPSO) for enhancing the efficiency of hybrid energy systems. FLPSO improves convergence rates and solution precision while maintaining resilience to complex conditions. By utilizing fuzzy logic to dynamically adjust PSO variables, it optimizes the distribution and consumption of diverse power sources in a grid-connected microgrid. Results show FLPSO reduces electrical power and battery replacement costs significantly compared to conventional PSO, saving ₹19,596.30 in fixed utility charges and ₹19,691.26 under flexible grid rates. Despite the challenges of battery deterioration, FLPSO outperforms PSO with enhanced sustainability, faster convergence, and lower operating costs, making it a more robust solution for energy management. Keywords: Microgrid Technologies, Fuzzy Logic-Built Particle Swarm Optimizations (FLPSO), Hybrid Systems for Energy Administration, Optimization Challenges, Battery Storages Deterioration, System Fluctuations.

articleTitle: High-Performance and Power-Efficient FPGA Accelerator for Adder-Based Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance and energy-efficient FPGA-based accelerator for Adder Neural Networks (ANNs), designed to address the computational challenges in IoT applications. By eliminating traditional multiplication-intensive operations and adopting an adder-based computation model, the accelerator significantly reduces power consumption, memory bandwidth requirements, and processing delays. A novel near-memory computation (NMC) architecture is introduced to minimize off-chip memory access, enhancing both speed and energy efficiency. Extensive evaluations on AMD-Xilinx VC709 and KV260 FPGA platforms demonstrate superior performance, achieving 96.3% accuracy, lower DRAM usage (by 45.5%), and 50% lower power consumption than CNN-based counterparts. These results position the proposed ANN accelerator as an optimal solution for real-time, scalable, and power-efficient AI-driven IoT applications.

articleTitle: Time Series Analysis and Forecasting of Vehicular Network Communication Severity: A Comparative Study of ARIMA and SARIMA Models
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The research evaluates vehicular network communication severity using two well-known statistical models namely ARIMA (AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average) and SARIMA (Seasonal ARIMA) for time series analysis and forecasting. The Bologna and Erlangen simulation datasets provide vehicular communication data to analyze especially packet transmission stops and communication interruption scales. The objective of this study investigates time-based dependencies and future severity prediction for transport networks to enhance reliability and performance of Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs). The data undergoes a complete exploratory data analysis (EDA) to reveal hidden patterns together with data trends and unusual data points. The results indicate that ARIMA and SARIMA models deliver accurate predictions yet SARIMA establishes a better ability to understand seasonal dynamics present in severity data sets. This investigation offers essential knowledge about time series models in VANET applications while presenting recommendations for vehicle communication system enhancement.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Deep Learning Framework with CBAM and TBAM techniques for Feature Fusion in Colon Cancer Classification from Histopathological Images
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Colon or colorectal cancers remain a significant global health problem, with a growing number of cases and increasing mortality rates. This paper presents a hierarchical deep learning classification approach for the detection of colon cancer, employing top-down and bottom-up strategies. The framework integrates EfficientNet models with high-performance feature enhancement techniques, including the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and Transformer-based attention mechanisms (TBAM), to improve feature extraction and classification accuracy. The model was trained and tested on a dataset of 25,000 histopathological images for improved accuracy. To analyze the efficiency of the proposed model, we used the performance metrics, including accuracy, G-Mean, F1-Score, Jaccard Index, Youden's Index and Diagnostic Odds Ratio (DOR). The experimental results indicate that the CBAM-based attention mechanism outperforms the Transformer-based attention model, with a classification accuracy of 87.42%, which proves CBAM's efficiency in enhancing deep-learning models for medical image analysis. The results of this paper indicate that the proposed deep learning model provides a robust and efficient solution for automatic colon cancer detection. By assisting pathologists in clinical decision-making, the model improves diagnostic accuracy, workload reduction, and timely and accurate cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: Face Restoration of Ancient Indian Statues using Image Inpainting
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Ancient sculptures of India are a significant part of our history and culture but at the same time, they get damaged because of human interference or environmental factors. Restoration of such statues, especially their faces, is highly necessary for the preservation of our rich cultural heritage. The traditional method is time-consuming and not precise. For this task, we proposed a machine learning-based technique to reconstruct missing parts of the sculpture faces from 2D Images with special focus on face reconstruction. In this work, our objective is to fill up the missing parts in facial area by using image inpainting techniques such as diffusion models. We have developed an algorithm where it detects the damaged area in the face of the statue and then applies binary masks and finally reconstructs the missing parts in the face and develops an accurate restoration of the face of ancient Indian statues. This is an easy-to-use system that allows the users to upload images of damaged statues, which are then processed by our algorithm to produce complete restored facial images. This innovative solution will help historians and archaeologists to revive our ancient Indian heritage more accurately and effectively.

articleTitle: Ensemble Transfer Learning Coupled Osprey Optimization Algorithm for Feature Selection from Skin Cancer Image Datasets
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Among different cancer diseases, skin cancer is one of the most common leading diseases that increases the mortality rate due to lack of adequate and timely treatment. The enhancement of technology helps dermatologists to use recent deep learning methods to identify diseases in the early stage to save lives of human beings. Different existing procedures have been performed with higher precision than naked eye inspections performed by dermatologists. Even if deep learning models have already been adopted for an easy and accurate diagnosis of the disease, they face different challenges, such as skin image segmentation, noise involvement while capturing the image, etc. This study presents a ensemble transfer learning coupled with an Osprey optimization algorithm to select significant features. The ensemble transfer learning concept is used for primary feature extraction to achieve better results. Later, the Osprey optimization algorithm(OOA) is implemented to select the optimal features. We access and compared the proposed methodology using a large-scale dataset of skin cancer. Support Vector Machine is used to figure out the performance of the ensemble TL - OOA. The experimental result shows the excellence of performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, specificity, and sensitivity. This ensemble TL - OOA has achieved a diagnostic accuracy of approximately 98.61%, precision of 96. 00%, sensitivity of 100%, and specificity of 97.62%.

articleTitle: Deepfake MRI Detection: A ViViT-Based Landmark Feature Extraction Approach for Brain Tumor Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Deepfake manipulation of MRI brain tumor scans pose significant risks, including misdiagnosis, fraudulent research, and ethical concerns in medical imaging. To address this, we propose a Video Vision Transformer (ViViT)-based deepfake detection model enhanced with landmark-based feature extraction, designed to identify manipulated MRI scans with high accuracy. Our approach adapts ViViT to analyze sequential MRI slices, capturing subtle inconsistencies introduced by deepfake techniques, while landmark-based features focus on key tumor regions for improved precision. Additionally, Depthwise Separable Convolutions (DSC) and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) are incorporated to enhance feature learning and computational efficiency. The proposed model is evaluated on the BraTS 2021 dataset, achieving a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 91.2%, Intersection over Union (IoU) of 85.7%, and an AUC-ROC of 98.4%, significantly outperforming CNN-based and GAN-forensic approaches. Based on the results, the proposed system exhibit higher accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Effective Energy-Selection Method for Heterogeneous WSN with Differential Power Sources Dependent on Node Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Advances in wireless communication technologies are constantly being made in many different fields, opening up new and better possibilities for general business systems. Large-scale deployments of tiny, light-weight wireless nodes are called wireless sensor networks (WSNs), and they are used to monitor systems or the surrounding environment. These sensor nodes must be better able to tackle increasingly complex tasks due to WSNs technology's increased compute capability. Wireless sensor networks, or WSNs, are a quickly emerging technology with a broad range of application services. A few of these services are provided to the academic sector, weather monitoring, traffic forecasting, surveillance, and research. Improving security metrics is the most exciting issue facing communication wireless networks today, since sensor nodes are dispersed randomly in wireless environments.SEP is an enhanced approach to LEACH in heterogeneous WSN that enhances life cycle. Therefore, because of the unequal energy consumption by the cluster heads and the nodes, the lifetime would be shortened. Reduce the energy usage of the cluster's nodes on the one hand by using intermediary nodes for indirect transmission. However, in order to lower the energy usage of cluster heads, include node energy in the CHE process. SEP is a heterogeneous-aware protocol that was created to increase the stability period—the amount of time that passes before the first node dies. Due to the requirement for consistent output from the sensor network, this characteristic is crucial for many applications. Based on the remaining energy in each node, the SEP determines the likelihood of each node becoming the cluster leader. After then, these probabilities are weighted. The results depicts that enhanced ESEP protocol is effective in balancing energy usage to increase the lifespan of the system when compared to the LEACH protocol, SEP protocol, enhanced Efficient-SEP protocol, and the MATLAB-proposed algorithm. Using advanced efficient SEP protocol with Cluster Head Election Method, the no of alive nodes are better than improved SEP protocol, the number of nodes are less than improved SEP protocol, and the consumption of energy of nodes is lower than improved SEP protocol.

articleTitle: Real-Time Pest Detection System Using Efficientnet Deployed On Raspberry Pi For Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: A real-time pest classification system is developed for this study with the help of Efficient Net architecture for precision as well as for resource efficiency. The hardware setup includes a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, 4 GB RAM, DC-to-DC Buck Converter (3A voltage regulator), 5MP Raspberry Pi Camera Module, and 16×2 LCD module. The system architecture includes a 12V adapter powering a buck converter that supplies the 5V needed for the Raspberry Pi and a VNC viewer that is used to access and execute the application remotely over a Wi-Fi connection. The model was pre-trained, and the stored model is utilized in the memory card using the transfer learning methods to optimize computation. Images are taken and preprocessed using the Raspberry Pi Camera Module and resized into a 50×50 resolution. However, robust model generalization is enhanced by using data augmentation techniques such as random rotations, flips, and even brightness adjustments. The architecture of the proposed training pipeline uses an EfficientNet model set with a batch size of 32, Adam optimizer, and a learning rate of 0.001. Thus, training is performed for 15 epochs, at the end of which the model attains a classification accuracy of 93.5%The LCD module presents the classification result, and also sends the prediction to the cloud-based server through API. The proposed system is a scalable low-cost solution for precision agriculture that would empower stakeholders in real-time detection of pests while minimizing crop loss. This paper demonstrates the system's effectiveness in a resource-constrained environment, leading to future enhancements including dataset expansion and edge AI deployment for localized decision-making.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Satellite Image Classification: A Comparative Analysis of CNN and ResNet-18
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: With the ease of classifying land through satellite imaging, remote sensing has captured the Earth observation domain.
