Traditional methods for analyzing satellite images relied on manual feature extraction and statistical models which was time-consuming and often failed to capture sophisticated patterns. Moreover, advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), have significantly improved classification accuracy. This study investigates the effectiveness of CNN-based architectures on the task of categorizing satellite images, by evaluating the performance of a custom CNN model against a pre-trained ResNet-18 model. The comparative analysis showed that ResNet-18 achieved better classification accuracy, computational efficiency and generalization ability than the custom CNN by achieving a 89.3% test accuracy with the reduced training time. These results indicate the power of transfer learning for the classification of satellite images and provide an efficient and practical means for the analysis of remote sensing data. According to the study, these deep learning classification algorithms isolate an effective and automated framework for handling large swathes of satellite imagery making it significant for environmental monitoring, land use planning, and disaster management.

articleTitle: Implementation Of A Cost-Effective Smart Grid Based On A Web Of Things To Access Multiple Energy Sources Remotely
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The growing world energy demand coupled with the constraint of fossil fuels requires a transition towards renewable energy sources. Wind and solar-based hybrid renewable energy systems have demonstrated efficiency in energy generation but are plagued by energy wastage. To overcome this challenge, this paper suggests a dual-energy generation system for integrated grids to improve energy efficiency and dependability. Load data from Rajasthan, India, have been investigated to create an optimized grid design on the basis of net present cost and unit cost of energy. PV tilt angle optimization, utilization of wind energy, and inverter efficiency are taken into account for stability of the system. Sensitivity analysis assesses the economic effect of variations in capital cost. A comparative analysis for Barwani, India, determines the PV–Wind–Battery–DG hybrid system to be the most economically viable and eco-friendly option. The suggested system brings innovations that make it more economically feasible, promoting consumer acceptance.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Powered Fall Detection and Behavior Monitoring Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Advances in modern medicine have clearly improved the human lifespan significantly. But elderly people have some problems in their life such as declining in movement ability due to getting old. They tend to suffer from reduced physical fitness, muscle weakness, decreased coordination, and balance problems. Such reasons lead to the fall, which sometimes leads to deadly consequences. This is particularly important if people live alone, where falls can come with serious health risks that require urgent assistance. Food and health care are also addressed, providing a description of solution-by-solution applications that tend to vary slightly depending on consumer best practices and risk functions, such as reaching out to the individual via phone to assess their condition prior to triggering emergency contact or medical attention should a fall be detected by a monitoring system. Thus, the birth of a new approach that would create a fall detection system that takes advantage of already available security camera video. This paper presents a system that tends to detect falls using computer vision and deep learning. It is trained to differentiate between activity type and fall type. The system incorporates additional functions including multiangle video analysis and multiperson tracking to improve accuracy and assess the severity of the fall, ensuring that urgent responses are prioritized. Enable Alerts for emergency contacts to alert contacts so they can assist a fallen person as soon as possible. This aims to raise living standards of life with a focus on preventing risks

articleTitle: Hybrid Predictive Framework for Expiry Date Estimation of Live-Attenuated Vaccines Using Stability Testing and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Transport sustainability is a major issue for most pharmaceutical agents, especially live-attenuated vaccines, which are highly sensitive to the environmental factors like temperature, humidity, light, and oxygen which is why there is need of of serious steps to be taken in the supply chain. In pharmaceutical supply chains, the most important part is to enhance the predictions related to stability for better storage and control over the inventory and minimized waste. Even though the supply chain helps us in tracking the Vaccine, the condition of it is still unknown. The stability of the vaccine is tested via these stability tests. Any deviation from the optimal order at any stage in the supply chain can compromise stability and make vaccines ineffective or unsafe. This study takes care of this by performing stability testing predicting the drug expiry according to the environmental factors. The predictive framework is a combination of machine learning regression models and the Arrhenius Equation to accommodate environmental variables affecting degradation. Ambient temperature and humidity were identified as the most significant environmental factors affecting degradation rates. The hybrid model comprising both ElasticNet and LSTM showed better prediction performance with a mean absolute error (MAE) cut off under 4.5% as compared to other conventional methods. For example, Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR) attained an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.85, the conventional methods scoring between 0.60 and 0.75. The model also accounted for a 12% decrease in the errors of expiration prediction when exposed to exposing temperature fluctuations during transportation. This is essentially intended to be produced in terms of standard recommendations for stability testing, which are crucial to the life cycle for the safe and effective use of medications.

articleTitle: IoT and WSN-Driven Solid Waste Image Classification in Smart Cities Using the Attention BiGRU Model
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Waste management has become an important issue in smart cities due to the dramatic increase in solid waste output caused by fast urbanisation and population growth. Inefficient garbage collection and disposal are results of using antiquated techniques in conventional municipal solid WMS. Modern technology advancements, especially in the field of solid waste image categorisation, are required to address the growing trash volume. The AtBiGRUCN model is introduced in this paper as a new DL that improves classification accuracy by combining RNNs, CNNs, and AM. In order to overcome obstacles in garbage can image processing, the model optimises feature extraction through the use of various combinations of shape, texture, and colour. To solve Text-CNN's positional feature loss problem, AtBiGRUCN learns spatial and contextual information effectively. Applying AtBiGRUCN with all feature combinations outperforms existing models, with experimental evaluations revealing a classification accuracy of 97.45%. Smart city waste management through solid waste image classification could be a promising area for DL, according to their results. More intelligent and automated garbage disposal systems are on the horizon, according to the suggested model's scalable and efficient solution, which will enhance sustainability and urban cleanliness in today's cities.

articleTitle: Driver Drowsiness Alert System using Machine Learning and Autonomous Car Parking
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This research tackles some of the critical challenges in vehicle safety and convenience by developing an integrated driver drowsiness alert and auto-parking system. Driver fatigue is one of the major causes of accidents, hence the need for real-time drowsiness detection. The proposed solution uses state-of-the-art computer vision techniques in the Python IDE to monitor driver alertness through the detection of prolonged closure of eyes for more than five seconds. Upon the detection of drowsiness, an alert is transmitted to the vehicle via the Blynk app. The vehicle, which is equipped with an ESP32 microcontroller, ultrasonic sensors for parking assistance, and an L298 motor driver for controlling movement, responds autonomously. It adjusts its trajectory by steering left and moving straight until it receives a stop signal from an RF transmitter connected to another ESP32 microcontroller. This system increases safety by preventing accidents due to drowsiness and improves convenience through automated parking. The integration of real-time communication and automation offers a robust solution to modern driving challenges.

articleTitle: Optimized ANN-GA Model for Predicting the Compressive Strength of High-Performance Concrete
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In new construction and when mixed with conventional concrete, there is a unique material called UHPC. Significant autogenous shrinkage, poor workability for large-scale production, high prices, and an unpredictable peak curing process are some of the obstacles that prevent UHPC from being widely used, despite its remarkable strength. Many large-scale restorations, strengthening projects, long-span bridges, and wet joint connections have made good use of its high compressive strength. Continuous hydration causes autogenous shrinkage to induce early-stage cracking by reducing internal humidity and increasing capillary tension, which in turn causes stress concentration and crack initiation. A new model for HPC modelling that combines ANN and GA is presented in this paper. While PCA chooses important features to feed into deep learning models, the model uses min-max normalisation for preprocessing. Before incorporating GA to find the best process parameters, an ideal ANN design is created utilising a BPNN with BR. When it comes to optimising parameters and forecasting penetration depth, the suggested ANN-GA model outperforms traditional approaches with an accuracy of 98.36%. In order to overcome obstacles in large-scale building projects and enhance HPC applications, this method shows how sophisticated computational approaches can be used.

articleTitle: Efficient Data Replication Management in the Cloud Using a Hybrid Meta Heuristics Optimization Model
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: A powerful paradigm called cloud computing, which shares information across the Internet, quickly serves the demands of companies and individuals. A data replication approach for data nodes is essential to maximizing load balancing and minimizing access time, ensuring data availability in large-scale cloud storage systems. This paper proposes a data replication management system in the cloud using a hybrid optimization strategy called adaptive pelican with butterfly optimization algorithm (APBOA), which combines pelican optimization algorithm (POA) and butterfly optimization algorithm (BOA) to select the optimal locations for replications and which files to replicate. The hybrid optimization balances exploration and exploitation to achieve superior performance, where the diverse cloud regions and storage options were explored using the pelican optimization and data placement, and cost efficiency and data placement replication frequency are optimized using butterfly optimization. The outcomes demonstrated that our method is effective and outperforms conventional approaches by achieving a less energy consumption of 1.15. So, the hybrid approach is cost-effective, more efficient, and dynamically adaptable to changing conditions in the cloud.

articleTitle: Hybrid Multimodal AI Framework for Real-Time Employee Activity Recognition and Workplace Motion Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In modern workplaces, finding a balance between employee productivity and privacy is a significant challenge. The Hybrid Multimodal AI Framework for Real-Time Employee Activity Recognition and Workplace Motion Analytics (HMAI-ERA) is a novel system that employs computer vision, motion tracking, and behavioral analysis to monitor employee activity in real time. The framework incorporates face identification (FaceNet & MTCNN), screen usage monitoring, mouse and keyboard activity tracking, and movement tracking to tag employees as "working" or "not working." Logs of activities with timestamps are saved in MongoDB for advanced analytics and visualization with an admin dashboard implemented using Flask. The framework also detects recurring mouse movement and idle screen usage to mark for potential anomalies. By combining several modalities, HMAI-ERA offers a non-intrusive yet effective way of monitoring workplace productivity. Experimental results indicate that the system can successfully monitor employee engagement with low false positives. The proposed framework offers a scalable, real-time, and privacy-aware solution for modern businesses seeking data-driven workplace insights.

articleTitle: Primary Tumor and Lung Cancer Prediction on Dual Energy CT Images for Nodal Metastasis using Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: One of the most important clinical responsibilities for lung cancer (LC) survival and recurrence is detecting lymph node metastases (LNM). It is still challenging to identify medical strategies and pretreatment choices for patients with malignancies based on preoperative identification of nodal metastases. The quantitative properties of shape, first-order, second-order, and higher-order textures in computed tomography (CT) are used to identify tumors. Statistical and machine learning (ML) studies are utilized to integrate clinical data and assess the attributes of their individual. This research discovered several radiomic features associated with distant, nodal, and histological spread, which has the great capability as an imaging biomarker for pathological diagnosis and target therapy selection. To detect nodal metastases (Nmets) from primary LC tumors, a new deep prediction approach with a Size-Related Damper Block (SR-DB) has been developed using Gemstone Spectral Imaging (GSI) dual-energy CT. In an implementation, a recommended strategy for Nmet prediction trained on the 40 keV dataset offers an accuracy of 0.89 percent and a sensitivity score of 0.95 percent. The results show that tumor heterogeneity and size aid in determining whether nodal metastasis from the initial tumor is absent or present in the proposed model.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electrical Power System(EPS) DC-DC converter Topologies for Efficient CubeSat Load Management
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: A CubeSat is a class of miniaturized and standardized satellites used primarily for scientific research, technology demonstration, and commercial applications. This research explores ways in which the efficiency of Electric Power System(EPS) of 3U CubeSats can be improved through the optimization of the operations of power converters, focus placed on boost and buck-boost converters. The EPS manages energy coming from the solar arrays, stored in batteries and delivered to loads. The research has realized the parameters defining power converter efficiency. These input and output voltages defined by arrangement of battery and solar cells as well as the switching frequencies. These improvements help maximize energy utilization by using maximum energy content in the solar panel to supply loads and batteries. To consider the effect of solar irradiance and temperature on the performance of solar arrays and batteries. A boost converter raises the voltage from the solar array for load and battery applications, while a buck-boost converter regulates the voltage for stability under variable input conditions. To use simulation and experiments to study the converter conditions impact system performance, dynamically managing loads to favour the distribution of energy for the most critical missions for CubeSats and promotes future improvements in small satellite power management capability toward long missions in earth observation and deep-space explorations.

articleTitle: FlexAssist: A Sensor-based Glove for Hand Function Assessment using MAS and QUEST
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Rehabilitation for hand motor impairments, such as those resulting from cerebral palsy or stroke, necessitates precise assessment and targeted feedback. This study develops a wearable device for hand rehabilitation that utilizes flex sensors, Arduino Uno, servo motors, and coin vibration motors. The device captures flex sensor data, records it in a CSV file, and processes it offline to classify spasticity and motor functionality. It applies percentage-based thresholds mapped to the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) and the Quality of Upper Extremity Skills Test (QUEST). The values after processing help with servo motor adjustments and vibration patterns to deliver feedback, this provides valuable insights for therapy. This cost-effective and portable system helps in addressing limitations of traditional rehabilitation methods and helps in enhancing sensor-based assessment to provide a scalable approach in improving hand motor function.

Author Keywords: Quality of Upper Extremity Skills Test (QUEST)

articleTitle: Blood Biomarkers for Knee Osteoarthritis using a Machine Learning Model with an Emphasis on Adult Patient
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic joint disease that reduces mobility and quality of life. Diagnostic procedures generally rely on imaging techniques, which frequently diagnose OA in advanced stages, restricting early management. The purpose of this study was to use machine learning (ML) techniques to find prospective blood biomarkers for the early identification of adult patients’ knee osteoarthritis (KOA). A strong prediction model was created by analysing a dataset of 2000 records. Machine learning to detect early OA using blood-based biomarkers such as CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, COMP and MMP-3. OA detection through Machine Learning Techniques. Normalization and outlier detection were used to pre-process biomarker data from a cohort of participants, which were then selected using correlation analysis and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). A Random Forest model was created, with an AUC-ROC of 0.92, Sensitivity of 0.85 and Specificity of 0.90, CRP and COMP emerged as major predictors of OA. These findings imply that combining machine learning with biomarker analysis provides a non-invasive, accurate and early diagnosis strategy, allowing for faster clinical interventions and improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of AI Algorithms for Real-Time IoT based Plant Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Plants are essential for sustaining life by providing oxygen, food, and maintaining ecological balance. Their growth and health depend on number of environmental factors such as soil moisture, humidity, temperature, and water availability. Traditionally, human intervention in plant care relies on manual observation, which can be insufficient and prone to errors. However, by combining AI, IoT and cloud computing technologies, this research enables real time monitoring and data driven decision-making, ensuring optimal plant health while promoting efficient resource utilization and sustainability. This study presents a comparative evaluation of AI algorithms for real time plant condition assessment using an IoT-based system. The environmental parameters like soil moisture, humidity, water level, and temperature of plants were utilized to analyze the plant conditions. Various AI models, including Random Forest, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and XG Boost, were trained to predict the plant conditions. Upon evaluation, Random Forest demonstrated the highest accuracy and reliability in predicting the plant needs. Consequently, this model is integrated into an IoT framework comprising a Raspberry Pi and respective environmental sensors like DHT11, Soil moisture sensor, Water level sensor. The system processes real time sensor data, analyses it through the trained AI model, and also stores it in a cloud and provides automated recommendations on motor activation when required. The cloud storage allows historical data tracking, performance analysis, and future improvements in predictive accuracy. This ensures efficient water usage while maintaining optimal plant health. The study emphasizes how well AI-powered decision-making works in precision farming and highlights the importance of model selection for improving prediction accuracy. The findings contribute to the advancement of smart farming technologies, demonstrating the potential of AI-IoT-cloud convergence in optimizing resource management and enhancing sustainability in agriculture.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Based model for single event upset current prediction in 14 nm FinFET
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: A surrogate model of Single Event Upset (SEU) transient current for circuit-level modeling is presented in this work using machine learning regression. The use of FinFET technology in defense and aerospace-integrated circuits has been made possible by its extraordinary success in terms of integration and performance compared to planar MOSFETs. Their susceptibility to radiation risks in these kinds of applications is still the main worry, though. In order for circuit designers to minimize radiation impacts prior to real manufacture, the semiconductor industry has refocused its efforts on device analysis prior to production due to recent technological advancements. The structure and device parameters are being designed using Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) tools. Nevertheless, these techniques require a lot of effort and processing. The viability of employing machine learning to forecast device characteristics and Single Event Transient (SET) current through an unsupervised learning technique is investigated in this work. The TCAD tool is used to create a 14nm 3D FinFET device, and a dataset with multiple parameters is produced. A feedforward neural network and a Random Forest Regressor model are trained using this dataset in order to forecast the SET pulse current. To test this technique and forecast SET current, a section of the 10% dataset was selected at random. The accuracy of the comparison between the actual and anticipated data is good. This demonstrates that TCAD can be replaced by machine learning models to speed up device performance assessment for large-scale circuits. In comparison, our suggested approach predicts the SET current in just 8–10 seconds. SET impacts can be lessened at the design process with the use of this study.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method of Assessing the Development of Alzheimer’s Syndrome through CNN/LSTM and PSO
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disease that has a substantial influence on society. Precise estimation of Alzheimer’s disease development is essential for prompt diagnosis and customized treatment. This paper proposes a hybrid model that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to improve prediction performance. The model examines the evolution of AD using a data-focused method, making use of an extensive MRI dataset with important neuroimaging variables. AD causes mental impairment and loss of memory, which complicates medical care provided to them. Data already in the public domain are used to predict future events or outcomes for forecasting that is essential for treating the disease. Conventional approaches, like CNN and LSTM, are useful for predicting the course of an illness because they can handle temporal patterns and spatial interdependence in datasets, respectively. Using the advantages of both methodologies, a new hybrid approach is proposed in this article. In order to optimize the hybrid model variables, this work employs Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), a highly efficient optimization approach to increase the accuracy of model forecasts. The hybrid CNN-LSTM model, with and without PSO, demonstrated accurate predictions of AD progression. Performance metrics such as F1-score, precision, accuracy, recall and ROC AUC were used to evaluate model efficacy. This research contributes to predictive analytics in healthcare, offering innovative solutions for enhancing patient outcomes in AD management.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Analysis of Modern PLCs: Exploring Data Logging and Performance Metrics Using the AXC F 2152
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of cyberattacks on Operational Technology (OT) systems, particularly those involving Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), has necessitated a closer examination of their cybersecurity capabilities. This study investigates the data logging functionalities of modern PLCs, with a focus on the AXC F 2152 from Phoenix Contact. By emulating PLC operations across three scenarios—normal operation, logging-enabled, and during cyberattacks—, the research evaluates performance metrics such as cycle time, memory consumption, CPU usage, and board temperature. Machine learning models were employed to assess the utility of collected logs in predicting malicious activities, highlighting the predictive power of diverse logging sources. The findings reveal significant performance impacts from logging and attacks, emphasizing the importance of optimized logging strategies. This work contributes to the field o f OT security b y providing insights into log-based defenses and the role of PLC performance metrics in enhancing cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Effective Task Scheduling based on Candidate Optimization Algorithm (COA) in Heterogeneous NoC-Based MPSoC
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Efficiency of the network communication and performance of the Network of Chips (NoC) with respect to the Quality of Service is greatly affected by the contention of the shared resources. Here, in this paper the design of MPSoC (MultiProcessor System on Chip) is done which is based on Network of Chips involves two steps – scheduling the sub tasks with respect to the Processing elements (PE) and further mapping the PE to the switching nodes which is present in the NoC topology. The evolutionary computation technique is applied once the development of the task model is completed to complete the first step which in turn helps in achieving less transfer cost as well as the running and execution time. The algorithm used in the proposed approach is the Candidate Optimization Algorithm (COA). Based on the NoC topology minimal expected network transmission delay along with less resource and power consumption is used to achieve the second step. The results obtained out of the comparison shows the resources and power consumption which is preferred by the COA algorithm in designing the system.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Model for Time-Series Groundwater Level Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Groundwater level forecasting is important for sustainable water resource management, especially in areas experiencing variable water availability. This research investigates the use of machine learning and deep learning methods to predict groundwater levels from historical data obtained from monitoring stations.The input data include groundwater measurements, temporal characteristics, and station information, which were preprocessed with interpolation and normalization techniques to ensure data quality.Different predictive models were deployed, such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Bidirectional LSTM. In addition, a hybrid model involving Random Forest with LSTM was built for leveraging both structured and sequential learning features. Model accuracy was approximated through Mean Squared Error (MSE) and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Score, with Random Forest being the most accurate in machine learning models (MSE: 0.0276, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>: 0.9946). Bidirectional LSTM was outperforming the simple LSTM with an MSE of 0.0848 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Score of 0.9835. The hybrid model had better predictive ability with an MSE of 0.0410 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Score of 0.9920.The findings indicate the efficiency of hybrid methods in improving prediction accuracy, with the implication that integrating machine learning and deep learning methods can enhance groundwater forecasting. Future research will aim to incorporate remote sensing data, utilize federated learning for decentralized processing, and investigate transformer-based architectures for additional accuracy enhancements.

articleTitle: Random Forest and Deep Learning Hybrid Model for Analyzing Steel Lattice Strength and Durability
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Strength necessitates structured arrangements of nano-sized interphase precipitates to save weight in HSLA steel vehicle structures. The composition of the alloy, the rate of ferrite formation, crystallographic structure, temperature, and the morphology and dimensions of precipitates influence interphase precipitation. Automotive manufacturers are pursuing lightweight chassis and bodywork to adhere to more stringent environmental regulations. Data preprocessing, feature extraction, and model training are advised for the investigation of steel lattice structural strength. Data is cleansed and organised for analysis during preparation. Fundamental characteristics are derived during feature extraction for classification. Binary classification with KRFDL algorithms and Spark distributed computing categorises normal and pathological occurrences. CNN and LSTM deep learning algorithms enhance classification by identifying atypical events like assaults. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method can classify alterations in steel lattice structures and their strength with an accuracy of 96.52%. The results illustrate how interphase precipitation enhances the strength and reduces the weight of HSLA steel. KRFDL and deep learning algorithms enhance the analysis of steel lattice strength in automotive material engineering. The method precisely classifies structural anomalies to assist manufacturers in optimising steel composition for performance and environmental adherence.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Smart Electricity Monitoring and Sustainable Grid System with Machine Learning-Powered Electricity Demand Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The increasing electricity demand and the utilization of renewable power sources bring to the forefront inefficiencies of conventional grids, such as inconsistent billing, transparency, and wastage of energy. This paper suggests the implementation of a blockchain-enabled smart electricity monitoring system integrated with machine learning-based demand forecasting. Blockchain provides safe, transparent transactions with no room for fraud and billing errors, while machine learning refines the distribution of energy through predicting the patterns of consumption based on LSTM and BiLSTM models. The envisioned system enables peer-to-peer energy exchange and real-time monitoring, cutting the cost of electricity and making the grid more efficient. Results from simulation illustrate enhanced accuracy of forecasting and security of transactions, showing the viability of a decentralized, green energy future.

articleTitle: Sentinel: An Integrated Framework for News Sentiment Analysis, Bias Detection, and Coverage Comparison Using LLMs
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The sheer proliferation of news sources online has resulted in a splintered media space, where readers are more often than not exposed to skewed reporting and limited perspectives. We present Sentinel, an AI-powered framework that relies on Large Language Models (LLMs) to facilitate sentiment analysis, bias detection, and coverage comparison. This would integrate an understanding of the emotional undertone, if biased at all, and the depth of coverage within all these news stories for the consumers. Our system incorporates web scraping, advanced NLP techniques, and custom algorithms to provide a comprehensive view on news articles. Going through the architecture, methodology, and real-world applications of the Sentinel, that is a product which has in it all the potential to empower its users in making ever better-informed decisions in the increasingly polarized media environment.

articleTitle: Utilizing Machine Learning Techniques for Predictive Modeling and Early Detection of Chronic Diseases
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of chronic diseases necessitates innovative solutions for early prediction and management. This study develops a machine learning-based system for chronic disease prediction, leveraging real-time data inputs and advanced computational models. The system integrates predictive analytics with user-friendly visualization tools, enabling accurate and efficient assessments of health risks. Using a dataset encompassing key health indicators, such as age, medical history, lifestyle factors, and physiological metrics, the study implements algorithms including Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Neural Networks to identify patterns and predict disease outcomes. Embedded programming and a graphical user interface (GUI) were employed to enhance accessibility, allowing users to interact seamlessly with the system for real-time analysis. The proposed model demonstrates high accuracy, with a prediction rate exceeding 90% for chronic diseases like diabetes, cardiovascular conditions, and hypertension. These results highlight the system's potential for scalable applications in clinical decision support and personalized health management, emphasizing the transformative role of machine learning in modern healthcare.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization based Explainable Deep Learning Models for Celiac Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Celiac disease is an autoimmune chronic disease, which occurs due to the ingestion of gluten, and affects about 1% of the world's population, diagnosed early in life to avoid potential damage afterward. Article on Particle Swarm Optimization-based explainable deep learning model for the prediction of celiac disease is discussed in this section. It applies PSO for feature selection and, therefore, does not offer redundant data to the extent of up to 35% with hyperparameter tuning that improves the efficiency of the model by up to 15%. The attention mechanisms along with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) would be incorporated in offering insights into the interpretable key genetic and serological factors making the predictions in the optimized deep learning model. It is experimented on some real datasets also, so as to get the validation on a large scale. Then, it also got 94.3% accuracy and resulted in 20% reduction of computation overhead. This approach makes clinical decision with good strong diagnostics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Skin Disease Classification Through GAN Generate Synthetic images for improved CNN Training and Generalization
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Every part of the world carries skin diseases which span from minor to potentially fatal conditions including skin cancer. Accurate early diagnosis of diseases depends on a time-intensive manual approach that shows errors frequently during the process. The proposed project develops an AI system to categorize skin conditions through deep learning using ResNet50 plus Random Forest as machine learning for image diagnosis alongside patient metadata examination. Explicitly the hybrid combined a CNN model to benchmark image classes while implementing Random Forest for metadata evaluation. The model benefits from enhanced generalization through GAN-generated synthetic images which help balance the dataset. The Streamlit-based web application enables users to upload images followed by diagnostic predictions output. The implemented system provides exceptional classification outcomes that allow medical staff to identify skin afflictions at the initial stage. The upcoming work plan consists of enlarging the present dataset while utilizing Explainable AI (XAI) methods and deploying the model on cloud services for simple access..

articleTitle: Multimodal Question Answering with DenseNet and BERT for Improved User Interaction
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) is a challenging AI task that combines computer vision and natural language processing to generate contextual answers from image inputs. It requires a model that is capable of comprehending both visual and textual information, generating correct reasoning and context-based predictions. The proposed model uses DenseNet to capture deep visual features and BERT to process questions so that image-text correlation can be interpreted more judiciously. With the ability to handle complex images and different linguistic structures, this system is most appropriate for education, healthcare, security, and accessibility applications, in which automatic question answering based on images enhances decision-making and user participation.Existing approaches, such as machine learning-based question generation, attention model, and Faster R-CNN-based methods, have drawbacks like inconsistent responses, high computational overhead, and scalability. The introduced model addresses the feature extraction process, increases contextual alignment, and maximizes training efficiency with learning rate scheduling and mixed-precision training, and it is a more efficient and scalable method than the current techniques.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Detection in Histopathological Images Using Lion Optimization Algorithm and Machine Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Lung cancer, a common malignancy in both men and women, requires early detection to reduce its severe impact. However, symptoms usually emerge in advanced stages, necessitating medical imaging for timely detection. Scientists have designed algorithms to identify lung cancer in histopathological scans. This study utilizes standard histopathological images from the Kaggle database. A computer-aided detection approach is implemented, beginning with an adaptive median filter for noise reduction and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to improve contrast in histopathological images. The Lion Optimization Algorithm (LOA) is then applied for feature extraction, where the extracted image intensity values serve as inputs for classification. Five classifiers—Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Naïve Bayes Classifier (NBC), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN)—are employed to distinguish between Benign and Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) cases. The findings reveal that the MLP classifier, integrated with LOA, attains a superior accuracy of 97.135%, as measured by established benchmark criteria.

articleTitle: AUTOAID: An Intelligent Accident Notifier
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Road accidents remain a leading cause of fatalities, injuries, and hospitalizations worldwide, primarily due to delayed emergency response and inadequate detection systems. This research paper explores advanced methods for accident detection, response facilitation, and safety enhancements to mitigate these challenges. By integrating sensor technologies, IoT systems, and real-time communication modules, the proposed solutions ensure timely alerts to emergency responders and individuals. The system employs accelerometers to detect abrupt changes in vehicle dynamics, vibration sensors to recognize collisions, and GPS-GSM modules for real-time location tracking. Alerts, including accident coordinates and timestamps, are sent via SMS or IoT-based platforms like Telegram to emergency centers. A feature allows cancellation of false alerts, optimizing response efforts. Our development has expanded the system to direct links to assistance services such as clinics, police, and fire stations. This integrated approach, supported by IoT data on distances, velocities, fuel consumption, and miles, demonstrates significant potential in saving lives and reducing accident impacts. In future, Additional functionalities could include monitoring helmet usage to mitigate head injury risks, detecting alcohol levels with MQ3 sensors, and leveraging fuel theft sensors at tank apertures. Overload risks are addressed using load cell sensors, while speed regulation can be achieved through turbine-based mechanisms emitting audible warnings at threshold velocities, A camera module may capture images post-collision, aiding in assessing accident severity.

articleTitle: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Phase optimization in Reflecting PMS beamforming
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is a linchpin in 6G communications. ISAC is enabled by identifying the targets followed by tracking the targets via communication. In supporting the tracking of targets, the Programmable Meta surfaces (PMS) beamforming reflection phases are optimized towards the target. Programmable capacitive PMS put forward uncomplicated antenna design with less energy utilization. In this paper, optimized beamforming in tracking targets is proposed by a Hybrid Quantum-Classical approach that utilizes the benefits of quantum algorithm that reduces computational time in generation of PMS phase dataset. Classical Optimization method stemming from Fourier transform approach in beamforming is augmented with Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) implemented to influence the optimal phase reflection with reduced computational time than classical optimization. The proposed method is validated with optimized beamforming towards multiple target scenario and shows the hybrid-quantum-classical model achieves 63.78% reduction in number of iterations with similar accuracy than traditional optimization in less computational time.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Faults in a Power System with Inverter Penetration Based on a Real-Time Machine Learning Application
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This study investigates the implementation of a machine learning (ML) algorithm for the classification and localization of faults in a power system with inverter penetration. The approach utilizes the Clarke transform and cosine distance prediction method to detect fault types and insertion distances. However, the results indicate that the general objective was not met, as the algorithm exhibited significant errors in fault classification, frequently predicting multiple fault types per observation, leading to indecisive fault identification. Additionally, the fault insertion distance detection showed poor performance, achieving only 36% accuracy with a tuned window of =1250. The study concludes that the decision criterion using L2 normal for characteristic eigenvalues and cosine distance for eigenvectors holds potential, but improvements in the regression model are necessary for reliable fault classification and localization in inverter-penetrated power systems.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Cancer Detection Diagonalizing with Texture Features Using the TexDiagNet Model
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Cancer diagnosis using medical imaging has witnessed significant advancements with the integration of deep learning. This study proposes TexDiagNet, a novel deep learning model optimized for texture feature extraction and classification in medical images, specifically chest CT scans. Using the publicly available Chest CT-Scan Images Dataset from Kaggle, the proposed method applies advanced preprocessing techniques to enhance image quality and emphasize regions of interest. TexDiagNet achieved an impressive accuracy of 97.10%, outperforming nine existing models, including NASNet (95.40%) and EfficientNet (93.80%). The model's training and validation losses were notably lower (0.10 and 0.12, respectively), demonstrating superior generalization capabilities. In addition to accuracy, the model excelled in other performance metrics such as precision (96.90%), recall (96.50%), and F1-score (96.70%). TexDiagNet's computational efficiency was also highlighted, processing images at 100 frames per second. These results suggest that TexDiagNet is a highly effective tool for diagnostic applications in cancer detection.

articleTitle: Advanced Multimodal Deep Learning for Predicting Cognitive Decline in Alzheimer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative condition that is progressive, is believed to be one of the big threats to global healthcare. Hence, there is a very severe need for early and accurate diagnosis. An advanced multimodal deep learning framework, which is based on DenseNet model and known for being dense in terms of its connectivity and reusing the same features, will improve the propagation of features and mitigate the problem of vanishing gradients. MRI scans from the ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) dataset have been used in this study for the experiment to predict cognitive decline and classify stages of it. The performance of DenseNet was also compared and evaluated with other models, among which there are several widely accepted models: CNN, VGG-16, and MobileNet. The results showed DenseNet had the highest test accuracy, which happened at 81.5% while the rest happened at less than 60% in detecting subtle neurodegeneration patterns associated with Alzheimer's progress, making it one of the most promising tools for the early stage of disease detection. This comparison may highlight the potential change that may be brought about by DenseNet in Alzheimer's disease research and later impact improved clinical results owing to timely intervention.

articleTitle: Improving Healthcare through the Internet of Health Things (IoHT): Continuous Monitoring of Patients, Data Analytics, and Interconnected Medical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The Internet of Health Things (IoHT) is a paradigm-shifting model for contemporary health care by allowing significant real-time patient monitoring via interconnected medical devices, wearable sensors, and data analytics. The Internet of Health Things (IoHT) technology bring together the advantages of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the healthcare systems, providing real-time, personalized care to patients and healthcare providers with timely and actionable insights. Through the selected literature studies, this research explores IoHT applications in the healthcare focus area, particularly the IoHT's potentials for continuous monitoring of patients' health status, processing large amounts of generated data using connected medical equipment, and improving clinical decision-making. As one of the new frontiers of clinical information systems design, IoHT consists of smart wearables, sensors, and diagnostic tools that capture critical health data in real time and share this information with healthcare professionals (HCPs) and care teams and connect them to enable tailored prevention, chronic disease management, and real-time care wherever the patient is located. By enabling predictive modeling, early disease detection, and personalized treatment plans using data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI), IoHT aims to enhance the efficiency of healthcare delivery. In addition, in the case of medical equipment which is highly inter-connected, communication between medical devices automatically contributes to higher patient safety, lower medical mistakes, and co-ordinated care. The IoHT ecosystem has potential, but it will be susceptible to issues such as data privacy and cybersecurity, interoperability, and heterogeneity issue, and integration of systems heterogeneous.

articleTitle: Harnessing Deep Learning Models in Fundus Imaging for Early Diagnosis in Eye Disorders
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Throughout the globe, eye conditions such as diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, cataract, and age-related macular degeneration are the major causes of blindness and visual impairment. Early detection is crucial to prevent permanent loss of vision. Fundus imaging is important for early detection of these disorders because it produces detailed images of the retina. The project aims to develop an automated system that can detect various eye disorders from these fundus images using deep learning. To build the model, a diverse collection of labeled fundus images was sourced from openly available platforms like Kaggle, EyePACS, and Messidor. These images were carefully prepared before training through processes like resizing, enhancing contrast, and applying basic transformations. The system employs a locally developed Convolutional Neural Network along with transfer learning-based ResNet50. The CNN model is designed to gradually extract important features from the images using standard building blocks like activation functions and pooling techniques, while also including methods to improve stability and prevent overfitting. The model was developed using the Django framework, along with user access to real-time diagnostic feedback through a web-based interface.

articleTitle: AI Based Threat Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: With the rapid growth of network cyber threats, there exists a growing need for advanced, scalable and highly accurate mechanisms for threat detection. AI based threat detection system is presented in this paper that uses machine learning and feature engineering techniques for classifying network traffic as normal to malicious. It leverages state of the art algorithms including Gradient Boosted Trees and a Multi-Layer Perceptron, achieving high accuracy with optimized preprocessing steps such as Principal Component Analysis and Chi Square feature selection. Learning techniques and feature engineering methods to classify network traffic as either normal or malicious. The system incorporates state-of-the-art algorithms, including Gradient Boosted Trees and Multi-Layer Perceptron achieving high accuracy through optimized preprocessing steps such as Principal Component Analysis and Chi-Square feature selection. A Flask application and Python GUI are utilized as a means to test the system via user friendly interfaces for real time prediction and validation.

articleTitle: ECNN-TDP: A Novel Convolutional Neural Network Model for Improved Thyroid Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Thyroid disease is among the most common endocrine illnesses and necessitates early and correct diagnosis to avoid serious health consequences. This paper presents ECNN-TDP, an Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network model that was designed for the enhanced classification of thyroid diseases from medical images and clinical information. The suggested model utilizes cutting-edge deep learning methods like transfer learning, attention mechanisms, batch normalization, dropout, and advanced activation functions to improve its prediction accuracy and generalization ability.ECNN-TDP is compared to benchmark models such as SCNN and TLCNN and is shown to perform better in fundamental measures of performance such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score—especially with larger dataset sizes. Although the model takes longer to train because it has a more complicated architecture, it makes up for this by making much quicker and more precise real-time predictions, rendering it an auspicious clinical tool.The findings affirm that the incorporation of contemporary deep learning techniques into CNN architecture significantly improves diagnostic efficiency for thyroid disorders. ECNN-TDP is a robust and efficient solution for early detection and classification of thyroid diseases. Optimizing its architecture further and verifying its performance in real-world clinical settings will be the focus of future work to maximize its potential in healthcare. Keywords: Thyroid Disease, Convolutional Neural Network, Deep Learning, Transfer Learning, Medical Imaging, Attention Mechanism

articleTitle: A DWT-Based Model with CNN-based Decision Fusion Strategy for Medical Image Encryption Scheme for Healthcare Network
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)

authors.preferredName: Osama Jamal Jamil Abed Al Jawad

abstract: Telemedicine and digital health are expanding rapidly, increasing the demand for secure and precise transmission of medical images. This study introduces an innovative hybrid model that combines DWT, CNN, and encryption techniques for safe image processing. The Proposed DWR-CNN model secures image embedding, hybrid encryption, and deep learning classification techniques. Medical images are concealed within a reference image using methods such as SVD to maintain their confidentiality while remaining unaltered. The image is subsequently transformed using DWT to enhance its resilience against attacks. A blend of AES and ECC protects the image transfer. VGG16 and YOLOv8 are to extract features and identify errors. The DWT-CNN model encourages precision and robust safety in evaluations using medical imaging datasets.

articleTitle: Decision Support System for Crop Planning and Agricultural Health using Machine and Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In order to ensure economic stability and food security, agriculture plays a vital role. However, farmers often find it difficult to make well considered decisions regarding disease detection with appropriate fertilizer or supplement suggestions for the detected disease, crop selection on the basis of rainfall soil health and location specific conditions. The Decision Support System for Crop Planning and Agriculture Health using Machine and Deep Learning Methods is a web application developed by utilizing a python framework named Flask is introduced in this study which employs Deep and Machine Learning models to assist farmers with three essential tasks: Disease detection with appropriate fertilizer or supplement suggestion for the detected disease, crop suggestion, and supplements and fertilizer purchasing section for known crop condition. Results from experiments prove the system's effectiveness in a range of agricultural domains, assisting farmers in boosting crop yield and ensuring timely disease remedy. This well-rounded strategy presents a feasible framework for revolutionizing modern farming practices. This Decision Support System ensures food security, pest control, crop production, better crop yield, better agriculture, economic growth, and good technology for farmers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity with Machine Learning to Strengthen Defenses Against Phishing Threats
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Increasing of cyber threats, Phishing attacks are to be remain one of the most continuing challenges in cyber security. Machine Learning is wondering in detection of cyber threats. This Research explored the different machine learning techniques which are helpful for detecting threats. Leveraging the different models such as Ensemble models and Deep Neural Networks. A comparative study of algorithms was conducted using the Real-time phishing datasets, and are been highlighted by their effectiveness in predicting malicious activities. The random forest model consistently outperformed comparing to the other models, achieving of 97.3% with Large Dataset and with small Dataset, it has achieved 98.5% with eminent features, while ensemble models demonstrated greater adaptivity to dynamic phishing patterns. This study also showed the importance of feature selection techniques, which includes domain heuristics and behavioral analysis, to improve the detection capabilities with the Limitations provided. Integrating real time threat intelligence and self-learning AI system are have discussed as keys for enhancing cybersecurity frameworks. Additionally, the Emerging trends such as Quantum Cryptography and adversarial machine learning are explored to future proof security defenses. The findings are contributing to the ongoing efforts to create robust, adaptive phishing detection, and robust mechanisms, and ensuring improved security for digital ecosystems.

articleTitle: Mechatronics Journey and Project Management of Arthropod Robots Design and Development
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Bioinspired design (BID) is revolutionizing mechatronics by integrating biological principles to enhance adaptability and efficiency. This study introduces a structured methodology—retrieval, mapping, and abstraction—to systematically translate biological phenomena into engineering innovations. Retrieval explores biodiversity to identify functional analogies, leveraging comparative methodologies for insight. Mapping converts biological mechanisms into technological applications, overcoming complexity through analytical models. Abstraction extracts core principles from biological insights, reformulating them into versatile engineering strategies. A bibliometric analysis of arthropod-inspired robotics demonstrates BID’s impact on mechatronic systems. Reviewing studies from over 30,000 publications, this research categorizes robotic constructs by operational environments—terrestrial, aquatic, aerial, and multimodal— emphasizing modular architectures and multi-axis articulation for enhanced adaptability. Insect-inspired designs dominate (53.8%), with significant contributions from institutions in the United States, China, Singapore, and Japan. Innovations such as origami-based deployable structures and direct-drive actuation affirm BID’s potential in applications ranging from planetary exploration to autonomous navigation. This study establishes BID as a foundation for next-generation mechatronics, driving advancements in robotic dexterity, efficiency, and resilience.

articleTitle: Enhanced Edge Detection and Segmentation Framework with Modified Yen's Thresholding for Parkinson Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Parkinson's Disease (PD) analysis is presently based on using accurate image evaluation strategies to identify pathological adjustments in images from MRI scans and DaT scans. Int his work, a new approach that exploits the combination of Gaussian Blur, Canny Edge Detection, Morphological Closing, and Modified Yen's Thresholding. The framework seeks to enhance the accuracy and reliability of PD analysis through a better fixed boundary separation of precise images. The preliminary processing step of Gaussian Blur is introduced to reduce noise and smoothen the image, at the same time as Canny Edge Detection is employed to discover edges correctly within the picture. Morphological Closing is a manner that makes the edges smoother through connecting the disconnected edges. Moreover, Modified Yen's Thresholding, a dynamic thresholding technique, determines the top-quality threshold values based on the neighborhood versions of depth, accordingly, it improves the accuracy of feature detection and segmentation. The evaluation of the proposed scheme becomes achieved on a dataset which covered 78 MRI scans and DaT Scans. The proposed work gives the accuracy of 91%, the precision of 88%, recall of 92%, the F1 score of 89%, and the low loss of 0.22. Thus the proposed model executed without over fitting and therefore it's far suitable for accurate and reliable PD diagnosis.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a convection-based diffusion model Biosensor for measuring water contamination in micro scale devices
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The research article explores the key factors influencing biosensor performance, particularly how the movement of target biomolecules affects detection efficiency. The work emphasizes the crucial yet often overlooked roles of diffusion, convection, and chemical reactions in sensor functionality. The research provides a detailed evaluation of various biosensor systems, estimating essential parameters such as flux rates, collection rates, and equilibration times. It highlights the importance of microscale and nanoscale sensors while addressing the discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental results, especially regarding collection limits and binding kinetics. A central focus is to target molecules move toward sensor surfaces. The authors propose a framework using dimensionless parameters to classify different operational regimes, helping predict sensor behaviour under various conditions. By examining the interplay between convection, diffusion, and reaction kinetics, they argue that a deep understanding of these processes is essential for optimizing biosensor design. To support their analysis, the authors present case studies on microscale and nanoscale sensors, comparing their collection efficiencies and equilibration times. They conclude that an effective biosensor design should strategically integrate transport mechanics and binding kinetics to enhance detection accuracy and efficiency.

Author Keywords: Diffusion and convection Target biomolecule movement

articleTitle: Enhancing Low-Power VLSI Design through AI-Based Simulation and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: AI and ML techniques have dramatically influenced rapid developments in low-power VLSI design with fast advancements in device simulations and power optimization strategies. AI-based simulation tools are now used for accurate modeling of power consumption, improving thermal analysis, and quickening design iterations through the detection of inefficiencies and optimization of energy consumption. In fact, this work focuses on some AI-enabled methods of power reduction techniques such as voltage scaling, clock gating, and leakage current minimization with respect to a sustainable VLSI design. Moreover, a synthetic dataset is created to mimic the actual power consumption trend in VLSI circuits so that predictive modeling and regression techniques can be used for power estimation. Different regression models are used to check the predictive accuracy, and it was found that the highest R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score was 0.85 by Linear Regression, while the worst was achieved by Decision Tree Regression at 0.50. Results of the correlation analysis and models by machine learning clearly indicate that the frequency and operating voltage are the major contributors to consumption power, while gate counts have a relatively insignificant contribution. Introduction of AI in VLSI simulation enables the enhancement of power efficiency while maintaining sustainability outcomes by optimizing energy usage and cost reduction in terms of computation.

articleTitle: An Adaptive LoRa based Forklift Tracking and Collision Avoidance System for Smart Warehouses
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This Forklift tracking and collision avoidance are vital in improving industrial safety and operational performance. The proposed Adaptive LoRa Based Forklift Tracking and Collision Avoidance (ALFTCA) based on Forklift Tracking and Collision Avoidance. The system works by adapting the LoRa transmission intervals dynamically depending on forklift velocity, obstacle proximity and geofencing regions to maximize energy efficiency and real-time tracking. The system uses GPS for location tracking, IMU sensors for detecting motion and ultrasonic sensors for measuring obstacle proximity. LoRa modules are used for low- power and long-range communication. When a forklift approach travels at high speeds, the rate of transmission goes up to real-time information. When low activity areas, it goes down to save power. The system is reviewing data and initiating collision avoidance features in the form of audio visual signals and performs automatic braking when the forklifts are within a critical distance. Experimental evaluations prove that ALFTCA is capable of cutting energy consumption by 27 percentage with tracking and safety warnings.

articleTitle: Leveraging Augmented and Virtual Reality in Conjunction with Artificial Intelligence, 5G, and Edge Computing to Transform Immersive Experiences
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: AR, VR, AI, 5G, and Edge Computing are converging to reshape immersive experiences across industries in terms of content creation, content delivery and content interaction. AR and VR have achieved remarkable progress so far in fields like the gaming industry, education, healthcare, and entertainment, and are already delivering immersive and realistic environments for users. Nonetheless, the real magic happens with their combination with AI, 5G and Edge Computing, which makes immersive experiences perform, scale and respond better to interactions. AI and AR/VR create a symbiotic relationship where AI designs intelligent interaction, personalizes user experience, and aids decision-making in AR/VR environments by analyzing user behaviors and context in real-time. Simultaneously, the rollout of 5G networks will provide ultra-low latency, high-speed data transfer, and immense connectivity, all of which are critical to rendering high-quality asynchronous immersive experiences. By processing data to the edge, close to the end-user, Edge Computing cuts latency to the minimal level and makes sure that interactions are fast and seamless enough to make immersive applications work. This paper discusses the convergence of AR/VR with the other digital technologies such as AI, 5G, and Edge computing and its impact on industries leading to more immersive, scalable and personalized experiences. In this report, we explore how these technologies make one another better, resulting in breakthroughs across fields like telemedicine, remote education, autonomous driving, and even virtual tourism. We also highlight the implications of this convergence in terms of data security, privacy considerations, and the requirements for computational resources. This paper encapsulates those concepts, discussing what comes next and what role immersive technologies will play in the next generation of human-computer interactions. Thus, the fusion of AR/VR, AI, 5G, and Edge Computing is enhancing user experiences while also enabling innovative and novel solutions for various applications and driving innovation.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Sign Language Recognition using Deep Neural Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Sign Language Recognition (SLR) plays a crucial role in facilitating communication for individuals with hearing and speech impairments. Advances in deep learning have significantly improved the automation of gesture recognition. There are many methods used to improve the performance of SLR. This paper evaluates the performance analysis of five models namely Custom CNN, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, Xception, and NASNetMobile on a benchmark dataset, employing preprocessing techniques and optimized training strategies. Among the models, DenseNet121 and Xception demonstrate the highest accuracy, while NASNetMobile offers a strong balance between performance and computational efficiency. The lightweight Custom CNN also delivers competitive results. Statistical analysis supports these outcomes, highlighting the importance of balancing accuracy, speed, and resource usage for practical deployment. Future directions include exploring transformer-based models, integrating multimodal learning, and optimizing for edge devices to promote more inclusive communication technologies.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Ensemble Model for Automated Severity Assessment of Osteoarthritis from Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This work aims to solve the difficulty of recognizing knee osteoarthritis using deep learning methodologies. Conventional methods of manual classification of osteoarthritis severity tend to result in an error when rated according to the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) degree a situation that complicates its utility in clinical practice. To address this problem, we are suggesting a strong framework using the most recent deep neural network approaches, namely InceptionV3 and EfficientNetB4, to improve the classification performance. In our study, we examine the performance of each model separately, defining the goal as identifying the correct Kellgren-Lawrence grade for the X-ray images of patients. We then explore how the models could be combined in an ensemble to gain the advantage of the strengths of both in their prediction task and enhance the accuracy. The results of our experiments show that the combined approach not only improves classification performance but also minimizes the risk of classification errors. The goal of this research is to present clinicians with a dependable tool in the form of deep learning methodologies to help diagnose knee osteoarthritis and ultimately improve the quality of treatment, thereby improving the patient’s quality of life.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Approaches for Efficient Brain MRI Segmentation: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Brain MRI segmentation plays a crucial role in the analysis of neurological diseases, offering insights into brain structure and aiding in the diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease, brain tumors, and multiple sclerosis. This process involves partitioning MRI images into meaningful regions or segments, typically identifying structures such as white matter, gray matter, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Traditional techniques like thresholding and region growing have largely been replaced by learning based approaches. Among these, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in automating the segmentation task, significantly reducing human error and increasing efficiency. However, challenges remain in handling diverse imaging data, managing noise, and ensuring robustness against variations in MRI scan quality. This paper explores various models that facilitate segmentation and details the implementation of the model that ultimately proves to be the most effective.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Sports Analytics: Unveiling Key Determinants of Olympic Success through Statistical Modeling and Innovative Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This study investigates improvements in sports analytics, with an emphasis on the Olympics, and uses statistical tools to identify significant performance determinants. The study uses Kaggle's athlete dataset to evaluate the impact of demographic and physical variables such as age, height, weight, and gender on medal success. Statistical procedures such as T-tests, Chi-square tests, and ANOVA indicate substantial differences between groups, including gender-specific patterns and differences in Summer versus Winter sports performance. Prior studies included limitations such as inadequate data, biases, and the inability to analyze underrepresented sports. The study also offers a sports suggestion app that uses augmented reality and wearable devices to provide personalized and immediate recommendations that adjust to environmental and individual variables. The methodology combines hypothesis testing, data preprocessing with IBM SPSS, and visualizations to derive actionable insights. Key findings include gender inequalities, with males averaging higher height (177.84 cm vs. 168.51 cm) and weight (74.43 kg vs. 61.14 kg), as well as seasonal variances, such as age differences between summer and winter sports. Medallists revealed distinct traits, with gold medallists standing at an average height of 177.28 cm and weighing 73.44 kg.

articleTitle: Automated Esophageal Cancer Detection using Convolutional Neural Networks for Early Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Successful therapy of esophageal cancer, Based on precise and timely detection, effective treatment of esophagus cancer, which is a highly severe condition, is possible. Traditional modes of diagnostic endoscopy and biopsy procedures are considerably time-intensive which leads to procrastinated diagnoses. With this in mind, attempts have been made to overcome these boundaries through the use of convolutional neural networks (CNN) for neural computation of esophageal cancer detection. The system employes both CNN and VGG-19 models for analyzing medical images that include both endoscopic and histopathologic images, as well as differentiating cancerous tissue from non-cancerous ones. The combination of feature extraction through CNN and classification of the images using the deeper network of VGG-19 results in enhanced accuracy of diagnosis and assists physicians in making better decisions. Steps of the proposed system are feature extraction, classification and image preparation. Others include model hyperparameter fine-tuning, such as augmentation, normalization, and resizing, which increases generalization and efficiency of the model. The CNN and VGG-19 architectures enable spatially and structurally patterns to be detected autonomously, thereby decreasing the need for manual feature engineering. Subsequent to the deeply learned features, the final classifier easily dicriminates between non-cancerous and cancerous images. The last classification layer allows for the rapid and accurate differentiation of images for cancerous and non-cancerous tissues. This new technique helps the pathologist and radiologist in making decisions by reducing the margin for error, speeding up the diagnosis, and merging with clinical routine. The use of CNN and VGG-19 in the detection of esophagus cancer has numerous advantages such as increased accuracy, speedier diagnosis, and lower reliance on human judgment. Technology improves the survival rate of patients by improving the early detection capabilities. Future studies may focus on the integration of clinical data and multimodal data for a holistic analysis, and could also make use of more refined architectures like ResNet or Inception for better results. This study allows for more refined methods of early intervention with the understanding that deep learning fundamentally changes how cancer detection is done.

articleTitle: Mechatronics in Solar-Thermal Evaporators: Technical Innovations from Asia to Enhance the Industry in Peru
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs) contribute significantly to global death rates.
