Likewise, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) estimated that each year, approximately 3.2 million individuals acquire HAIs, leading to around 37,000 fatalities. This underscores the need for efficient sterilization methods. In response, China has developed sustainable solar thermal autoclave technologies that utilize renewable energy, reducing operational costs and CO₂ emissions. This study conducted a literature review on solar-thermal evaporators technologies developed over the past decade, analyzing patents and prototypes in terms of energy efficiency, achieved temperature, and potential medical applications. Additionally, Peruvian regions with high solar radiation were identified using data from the Global Solar Atlas. The evaluated models include autoclaves with graphene membranes, bioinspired structures, and steam generators with copper tubes. These technologies achieved efficiencies of up to 87.43% and temperatures exceeding 132 °C. Finally, five hospitals in regions with high solar radiation (Arequipa, Moquegua, Tacna, Puno, and Ayacucho) were proposed for the implementation of these solutions, enhancing the sustainability of the healthcare system. The incorporation of solar autoclaves in Peru could optimize energy resources and reduce costs, fostering a more sustainable healthcare system. Further research should conduct studies on solar radiation in specific hospitals and adapt Chinese technologies to local needs, promoting investment and the development of innovative medical solutions in the region.

articleTitle: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Based on Optimal Feature Selection Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: A neurodevelopmental disorder autism spectrum disorder (ASD) still remains a challenge among research fields, and the current diagnostic procedures still need to be improvised for more precise detections. Although several investigations by involving the usage of different machine learning (ML) algorithms toward the identification of ASD among individuals, there is still a large gap in optimizing feature selection methods toward better accuracy and efficiency. Systematic comparisons among various feature selection methods are rather neglected in prior studies, so there is less potential for discovering the best diagnostic markers. In this light, our work brings forth a comprehensive framework that investigates three different kinds of feature selection methods-mutual information, wrapper-based selection by Random Forest, and LASSO regularization by XGBoost. Our methodology implements structured evaluations toward the assessment of the impact of each tool for the identification of detecting accuracy and computation. Also, comparative evaluation results that though wrapper-based selection increased the first model’s accuracy up to 90%, the use of XGBoost with LASSO regularization outperformed it with an accuracy of 99.8%. Results establish the importance of our approach in streamlining clinical assessment processes and identifying features about ASD that are crucial towards advancing data-driven detection methodologies.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Driven Smart Signal Systems for Advanced Image and Video Processing in Urban Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The increasing integration of intelligent systems in metropolitan environments emphasizes the important role effective image and video processing performs in applications including the traffic management, the monitoring of safety, and the urban planning. When handling dynamic scenarios, that is, changes in traffic conditions, occlusions, and the need for real-time analysis, conventional signal processing methods sometimes fail. Strong and adaptable solutions able to manage both these complexity as well as others are thus much needed. This work intends to introduce a deep learning-based smart signal system designed to process real-time video feeds for uses connected to urban traffic and safety. The proposed system uses recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for temporal sequence comprehension; conversely, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are used for spatial data analysis. Two approaches used in order to improve the performance of the model are data augmentation and transfer learning, which increase the accuracy of decision-making using multi-modal data sources, video streams, sensor inputs, environmental parameters. This helps one to get beyond the challenge of small datasets. System performance is discovered using benchmark datasets and video from actual traffic events. Better than the methods now in use, the results show object detection has 95% accuracy and anomaly detection has 92% accuracy. Promising for use in smart cities, the proposed framework exhibits scalability and flexibility over a wide range of events. Its characteristics, traffic optimization, safety monitoring, and data-driven urban planning, which comprise traffic control, safety monitoring, and data-driven urban planning, have the ability to drastically change urban transportation infrastructure management.

articleTitle: Applying Machine Learning to Economic Analysis: Predicting Bank Failures in India Using Decision Tree Models
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This study examines the application of machine learning (ML) techniques, specifically decision trees (DTs), to predict the financial stability of institutions. Using the C5.0 algorithm, a DT was constructed and tested on a dataset, achieving an accuracy of 89.7%. Key financial indicators, including financial margin and profitability of assets, were identified as the most influential in determining success or failure. The findings highlight the effectiveness of DTs in economic forecasting, demonstrating their potential for financial risk assessment. However, limitations such as data availability, the lack of time-series analysis, and the model's inability to learn incrementally were identified. Despite these challenges, the results suggest that DTs can serve as a valuable tool for financial decision-making. Future research can refine the model by incorporating additional economic variables and exploring alternative ML algorithms to improve predictive accuracy.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Learning with Variational Autoencoders for Anomaly Detection in Autonomous Drone Fleets
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: However, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly being employed for different applications such as surveillance, logistics, disaster response, and smart city management, and thereby, the requirement for robust detection of anomalies and path optimization techniques has arisen. Existing traditional UAV monitoring systems typically depend on anomaly detection based on a rule or an unsupervised clustering method, i.e., DBSCAN and One-Class SVM, balancing high false positives and slow response time, correction, and suboptimal trajectory. To tackle these issues, we develop an AI-powered UAV anomaly detection and adaptive navigation framework where Isolation forests and MDPs are used to predict UAV trajectory, and DQNs are used for adaptive navigation. Experimental results in a simulated smart city arena with a multi-UAV fleet show that our proposed framework achieves 94% accuracy, 92% precision, and 91% recall, which are much superior to the existing approaches, such as One Class SVM (87% accuracy) and DBSCAN (80% accuracy). Additionally, the system compensates for false positives by 30%, improves energy efficiency by 15%, and reduces UAV collision risks by 20%, with high compatibility with real-time UAV fleet management. In the future, the scalability and the adaptability of the UAV-based smart city operation will be furthered through federated learning-based decentralised UAV coordination, reinforcement learning for autonomous swarm intelligence, and hybrid optimisation techniques for improving energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emergency Response with Real-Time Video Analytics for Natural Disaster Management
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Natural disasters pose severe risks to human life and infrastructure, necessitating efficient and rapid response systems. Traditional disaster response mechanisms often struggle with delays in data acquisition and processing, hindering effective management. The unpredictability and variability of disasters require timely and accurate responses, which are often compromised by latency issues in current management systems that largely depend on manual reporting and satellite data. We introduce an advanced disaster management system utilizing real-time video analytics powered by deep learning to enhance the speed and accuracy of emergency responses. This system integrates live video feeds from various sources with AI-driven analytics to identify and classify disaster events instantaneously. The system is trained on a comprehensive dataset consisting of varied disaster scenarios captured through video and images, annotated for different types of disasters such as floods, fires, and earthquakes. This dataset enables the model to recognize and react to a variety of disaster events accurately. Preliminary results demonstrate the system’s ability to classify disaster types with an accuracy of 95%, significantly reduce response times, and maintain a precision of 91.8%. The continuous monitoring and real-time updates from the system enhance situational awareness and decision-making during crises. The proposed system illustrates the potential of integrating AI with emergency management practices, showcasing significant improvements in response times and accuracy. With a demonstrated high accuracy and precision, this approach not only saves lives but also reduces economic losses by enabling quicker and more effective disaster response strategies.

articleTitle: Intelligent Resume Parser and Classifier Using Regular Expressions
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper presents a Resume Parser and Classifier that effectively extracts key details and classifies resumes by integrating compiler design concepts like regular expressions with Machine learning(ML) models. The system has two phases: Lexical Analysis and Classification. Lexical analysis is done using regular expressions to extract key details like name, contact information, skills, and education. By converting these details into feature vectors using TF-IDF and One-hot encoding, two datasets are created. By converting the extracted text from resume images into Word2Vec embeddings, a third dataset is created. A comparative analysis is done between datasets and models by giving the datasets as input to five ML models: RF, SVM, KNN, XGB and LGBM. These models predict the most suitable job role from 14 classes. To handle class imbalance, SMOTE is applied. PCA is employed for reducing dimensionality in order to find the optimal number of components. The system is evaluated using accuracy and f1-score as performance metrics. RF has proven to be the best model with an accuracy of 98.29% and Fl-Score of 98.30%. The combination of traditional compiler design principles for preparing the datasets with ML provides an effective tool for resume parsing and classification, offering a reliable and feasible solution to aid recruiters by accurately matching candidates to job roles.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality Based Therapy App for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative and sophisticated Augmented Reality application for use in children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis support therapy. The idea of using AR's innovative competence features to offer customised environments involving and interesting to the kids will be helpful in promoting their development of social, communication, and adaptive skills. Through the use of the SCERTS framework and adaptive learning features, the system tailors tasks according to individual performance, both in terms of usability and therapeutic impact. Preliminary feedback from therapists and parents shows enhanced interaction and visible behavioural growth. Future developments involve increasing environment variety, incorporating machine learning for dynamic adaptation, and facilitating greater accessibility through multilingual and wearable device support.
